title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 134 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 628–639 (Night 134, continuing directly from nights-133), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. Four verse lines on p. 636 are printed in broken type in the copy used; six words there could not be read and are shown as […]. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 134 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. Dunyā answers Tāj al-Mulūk's letters with threats in verse; his last, written for him by ʿAzīz, calls down a curse on her, and she has her old nurse beaten and thrown out of the palace. The nurse explains to the prince why Dunyā hates men — a dream of two doves, in which the female freed her mate from a fowler's net but the male abandoned her when she was caught — and the vizier has a pavilion in Dunyā's garden painted with the dream, finished so that the male is seized by a bird of prey before he can come back. Seeing it, Dunyā softens; she glimpses Tāj al-Mulūk walking below and falls in love, and the nurse smuggles him into the palace dressed as a slave-girl. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ وَالثَّلٰثُونَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-rābiʿatu wa-al-thalāthūna baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fourth and the thirty after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and thirty-fourth night,
sentences.n: The print spells thalāthūn without its long alif (والثلثون); the small alif over the lām is ours, to show the long vowel.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ لَمَّا بَكَى قَالَتْ لَهُ الْعَجُوزُ طِبْ نَفْسًا وَقَرَّ عَيْنًا فَلَا بُدَّأَنْ أُبَلِّغَكَ مَقْصُودَكَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna tāja al-mulūki lammā bakā qālat lahu al-ʿajūzu ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan fa-lā budda an uballighaka maqṣūdaka
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that Tāj al-Mulūk, when he wept, the old woman said to him: Be good of soul and cool of eye, for there is no escape (but) that I make-you-reach your aim.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when Tāj al-Mulūk wept, the old woman said to him, “Cheer up and be easy, for I will certainly get you what you are after.”
sentences.n: The night picks up the last words of the night before and repeats them. The sentence begins with Tāj al-Mulūk and then changes course (anna tāja al-mulūki lammā bakā qālat lahu al-ʿajūz, “that Tāj al-Mulūk, when he wept, the old woman said to him”), a loose construction common in the Nights. ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan, “be good of soul and cool of eye”: “take heart, be content”. The print sets lā budda an as لا بدان, joining budda to an.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَتْ وَتَرَكَتْهُ عَلَى النَّارِ وَتَوَجَّهَتْ إِلَى السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا فَرَأَتْهَا مُتَغَيِّرَةَ اللَّوْنِ مِنْ غَيْظِهَا بِمَكْتُوبِ تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāmat wa-tarakathu ʿalā al-nāri wa-tawajjahat ilā al-sayyidati dunyā fa-raʾathā mutaghayyirata al-lawni min ghayẓihā bi-maktūbi tāji al-mulūki
sentences.l: Then she rose and left him upon the fire, and headed to the Lady Dunyā, and saw her changed of the colour from her rage at the letter of Tāj al-Mulūk.
sentences.i: Then she got up and left him on hot coals, and went to the Lady Dunyā, and found her pale with rage at Tāj al-Mulūk's letter.
sentences.n: tarakathu ʿalā al-nār, “she left him on the fire”: in a fever of anxious waiting. mutaghayyirat al-lawn, “changed of colour”. bi-maktūbi, “at the letter”: bi- gives the cause of her rage.

sentences.t: فَنَاوَلَتْهَا الْكِتَابَ فَازْدَادَتْ غَيْظًا وَقَالَتْ لِلْعَجُوزِ أَمَا قُلْتُ لَكِ إِنَّهُ يَطْمَعُ فِينَا
sentences.tr: fa-nāwalathā al-kitāba fa-izdādat ghayẓan wa-qālat li-al-ʿajūzi a-mā qultu laki innahu yaṭmaʿu fīnā
sentences.l: And she handed her the letter, and she increased (in) rage, and said to the old woman: Did I not say to you that he covets us?
sentences.i: She handed her the letter, and Dunyā grew angrier still and said to the old woman, “Didn't I tell you he has designs on us?”
sentences.n: ṭamiʿa fī, “to covet, to set one's hopes on”. Dunyā speaks of herself as “us”, the plural of dignity.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا وَأَيُّ شَيْءٍ هَذَا الْكَلْبُ حَتَّى يَطْمَعَ فِيكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā wa-ayyu shayʾin hādhā al-kalbu ḥattā yaṭmaʿa fīki
sentences.l: And she said to her: And what thing (is) this dog, that he should covet you?
sentences.i: The old woman said to her, “And what is this dog, that he should have designs on you?”
sentences.n: ayyu shayʾin, “what thing”: Middle Arabic for “what?”. The print marks ayy with its doubling sign (وايّ) and gives fīki its kasra, “you” (feminine).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا اذْهَبِى إِلَيْهِ وَقُولِي لَهُ إِنْ رَاسَلْتَهَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ضَرَبَتْ عُنُقَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā al-sayyidatu dunyā idhhabī ilayhi wa-qūlī lahu in rāsaltahā baʿda dhālika ḍarabat ʿunuqaka
sentences.l: And the Lady Dunyā said to her: Go to him and say to him: If you correspond-with her after that, she struck your neck.
sentences.i: The Lady Dunyā said to her, “Go to him and tell him: ‘If you write to her ever again, she will have your head struck off.’”
sentences.n: After in, “if”, the past tense serves for the future in both halves: ḍarabat, “she struck”, means “she will strike”. ḍaraba ʿunuqahu, “to strike someone's neck”, is to behead him. We read ḍarabat, “she”, since the message is to be passed on about Dunyā; ḍarabtu, “I”, as if Dunyā spoke to him directly, is also possible. The print spells idhhabī with a final ى (اذهبى).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا الْعَجُوزُ اكْتُبِي لَهُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ فِي مَكْتُوبٍ وَأَنَا آخُذُ الْمَكْتُوبَ مَعِي لِأَجْلِ أَنْ يَزْدَادَ خَوْفُةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā al-ʿajūzu uktubī lahu hādhā al-kalāma fī maktūbin wa-anā ākhudhu al-maktūba maʿī li-ajli an yazdāda khawfuhu
sentences.l: And the old woman said to her: Write to him this speech in a letter, and I take the letter with me, for the sake that his fear increase.
sentences.i: The old woman said to her, “Write this to him in a letter, and I will take the letter with me, so that he will be all the more afraid.”
sentences.n: li-ajli an, “for the sake of (it) that”: “so that”. The print writes the pronoun -hu of khawfuhu, “his fear”, with a final tāʾ marbūṭa (خوفة), a habit of this edition; read -hu.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْ وَرَقَةً وَكَتَبَتْ فِيهَا هَذِةِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhat waraqatan wa-katabat fīhā hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And she took a paper and wrote in it these verses:
sentences.i: So Dunyā took a sheet of paper and wrote these verses on it:
sentences.n: The print spells hādhihi, “these”, with a final tāʾ marbūṭa (هذة), as it often does.

sentences.tr:
ayā ghāfilan ʿan ḥādithāti al-ṭawāriqi * wa-laysa ilā nayli al-wiṣāli bi-sābiqi
a-tazʿumu yā maghrūru an tudrika al-suhā * wa-mā anta li-al-badri al-munīri bi-lāḥiqi
fa-kayfa tuʾammilunā wa-tarjū wiṣālanā * li-taḥẓā bi-ḍammin li-al-qudūdi al-rawāshiqi
fa-daʿ ʿanka hādhā al-qaṣda khīfata saṭwatī * bi-yawmin ʿabūsin fīhi shaybu al-mafāriqi
sentences.l:
O heedless of the happenings of the night-comers, * and (who) is not, to the attaining of the union, a forerunner!
Do you claim, O deluded one, that you reach al-Suhā, * when you are not, to the full-moon the shining, a catcher-up?
So how do you hope-in us and hope for our union, * to win an embrace of the statures the slender?
So leave off from you this aim, (in) fear of my assault * on a day frowning, in it the greying of the partings.
sentences.i:
You who never heed the blows that come by night, * and will never be first to win your way to union:
Do you think, deluded man, to reach the faintest star, * when you cannot even catch the shining moon?
How can you set your hopes on me and long for my love, * thinking to clasp a slender, graceful form?
Give up this aim of yours, for fear of my wrath * on a day so grim it turns the hair grey at the parting.
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. al-ṭawāriq, “the night-comers”, are misfortunes that strike by night. bi-sābiqi and bi-lāḥiqi: bi- after a negative (laysa, mā) only strengthens it. al-Suhā is a faint star in the Great Bear, used to test keen eyes, and so the type of the unreachable; the full moon (al-badr) is the easy mark he cannot reach either. Dunyā speaks of herself as “us” (tuʾammilunā, wiṣālanā). qudūd, “statures, figures”, rawāshiq, “slender, graceful”. khīfata, “for fear of”, gives the reason. yawmun ʿabūs, “a frowning day”, is a Qurʾānic phrase (76:10); mafāriq are the partings of the hair, where greyness first shows.
sentences.t:
اَيَا غَافِلاً عَنْ حَادِثَاتِ الطَّوَارِقِ * وَلَيْسَ اِلى نَيْلِ الْوِصَالِ بِسَابِقِ
اَتَزْعُمُ يَا مَغْرُورُ اَنْ تُدْرِكَ السُّهَا * وَمَا اَنْتَ لِلْبَدْرِ الْمُنِيرِ بِلَاحِقِ
فَكَيْفَ تُؤَمِّلُنَا وَتَرْجُو وِصَالَنَا * لِتَحْظَى بِضَمٍّ لِلْقُدُودِ الرَّوَاشِقِ
فَدَعْ عَنْكَ هَذَا الْقَصْدَ خِيفَةَ سَطْوَتِي * بِيَوْمٍ عَبُوسٍ فِيهِ شَيْبُ الْمَفَارِقِ
ثُمَّ طَوَتِ الْكِتَابَ وَنَاوَلَتْهُ لِلْعَجُوزِ فَأَخَذَتْهُ وَانْطَلَقَتْ بِهِ إِلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭawati al-kitāba wa-nāwalathu li-al-ʿajūzi fa-akhadhathu wa-inṭalaqat bihi ilā tāji al-mulūki
sentences.l: Then she folded the letter and handed it to the old woman; and she took it and went off with it to Tāj al-Mulūk.
sentences.i: Then she folded the letter and handed it to the old woman, who took it and set off with it to Tāj al-Mulūk.
sentences.n: nāwalathu li-al-ʿajūz, “she handed it to the old woman”: Classical nāwala takes two objects; the li- is Middle Arabic. inṭalaqat bihi, “she went off with it”: bi- of accompaniment.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا قَامَ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَا أَعْدَمَنِى اللَّهُ بَرَكَةَ قُدُومِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā qāma ʿalā qadamayhi wa-qāla lā aʿdamanī allāhu barakata qudūmiki
sentences.l: And when he saw her, he stood on his two feet and said: May God not deprive me (of) the blessing of your coming!
sentences.i: When he saw her he rose to his feet and said, “May God never deprive me of the blessing of your visits!”
sentences.n: lā aʿdamanī allāh, “may God not deprive me”: lā with the past tense makes a wish. The print spells aʿdamanī with a final ى (اعدمنى).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْعَجُوزُ خُذْ جَوَابَ مَكْتُوبِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-ʿajūzu khudh jawāba maktūbika
sentences.l: And the old woman said to him: Take the answer of your letter.
sentences.i: The old woman said to him, “Here is the answer to your letter.”

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الْوَرَقَةَ وَقَرَأَهَا وَبَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَقَالَ إِنِّي أَشْتَهِي مَنْ يَقْتُلُنِي الْآنَ حَتَّى أَسْتَرِيحَ فَإِنَّ الْقَتْلَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيَّ مِنْ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ الَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-waraqata wa-qaraʾahā wa-bakā bukāʾan shadīdan wa-qāla innī ashtahī man yaqtulunī al-āna ḥattā astarīḥa fa-inna al-qatla ahwanu ʿalayya min hādhā al-amri alladhī anā fīhi
sentences.l: And he took the paper and read it, and wept a weeping strong, and said: Indeed I desire (one) who kills me now, so that I rest; for the killing (is) easier upon me than this matter which I (am) in it.
sentences.i: He took the paper and read it and wept bitterly, and said, “I wish someone would kill me now and give me rest, for death would be easier for me than this state I am in.”
sentences.n: ishtahā, “to desire, to crave”, in Middle Arabic simply “to want, to wish for”. ahwanu ʿalayya, “easier upon me”: the print marks ʿalayya with its doubling sign (عليّ).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَ دَوَاةً وَقَلَمًا وَقِرْطَاسًا وَكَتَبَ مَكْتُوبًا وَرَقَمَ فِيهِ هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadha dawātan wa-qalaman wa-qirṭāsan wa-kataba maktūban wa-raqama fīhi hādhayni al-baytayni
sentences.l: Then he took an inkwell and a pen and a paper, and wrote a letter, and inscribed in it these two verses:
sentences.i: Then he took inkwell, pen and paper and wrote a letter, setting down in it these two verses:
sentences.n: raqama, “to inscribe, to write out”, a more elegant word than kataba.

sentences.tr:
fa-yā munyatī lā tabtaghī al-hajra wa-al-jafā * wa-zūrī muḥibban fī al-maḥabbati ghāriqu
wa-lā taḥsabīnī fī al-ḥayāti maʿa al-jafā * fa-rūḥī min baʿda al-aḥibbati ṭāliqu
sentences.l:
So O my wish, do not seek the desertion and the harshness, * and visit a lover (who is) in the love drowning;
And do not reckon me (to be) in the life with the harshness: * for my spirit, after the beloveds, (is) divorced.
sentences.i:
My heart's desire, do not seek to shun me and be cruel; * come visit a lover who is drowning in his love.
Do not think I can live on while you are cruel: * once my loved ones are gone, my soul is divorced from me.
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. lā tabtaghī, “do not seek”, is the feminine jussive: here, unlike Dunyā's poem, the beloved is addressed as a woman. The print points ghāriqu, “drowning”, in the nominative for the rhyme, where muḥibban would lead one to expect ghāriqan; read it as “who is drowning”. al-ḥayāt, “life”, is printed with wāw (الْحَيَوةِ). min baʿda is printed with fatḥa where baʿdi is expected after min. ṭāliq, “divorced”, is the word for a repudiated wife: his soul will part from him as a divorced wife leaves her husband.
sentences.t:
فَيَا مُنْيَتِي لَا تَبْتَغِي الْهَجْرَ وَالْجَفَا * وَزُورِي مُحِبًّا فِي الْمَحَبَّةِ غَارِقُ
وَلَا تَحْسَبِينِي فِي الْحَيَوةِ مَعَ الْجَفَا * فَرُوحِي مِنْ بَعْدَ الْاَحِبَّةِ طَالِقُ
ثُمَّ طَوَى الْكِتَابَ وَأَعْطَاةُ لِلْعَجُوزِ وَقَالَ لَهَا لَا تُوَأخِذِينِى فَقَدْ أَتْعَبْتُكِ بِدُونِ فَائِدَةٍ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭawā al-kitāba wa-aʿṭāhu li-al-ʿajūzi wa-qāla lahā lā tuwākhidhīnī fa-qad atʿabtuki bi-dūni fāʾidatin
sentences.l: Then he folded the letter and gave it to the old woman and said to her: Do not blame-me, for I have wearied you without profit.
sentences.i: Then he folded the letter and gave it to the old woman, saying, “Forgive me, for I have put you to all this trouble for nothing.”
sentences.n: The print writes the pronoun of aʿṭāhu, “he gave it”, with a final tāʾ marbūṭa (اعطاة); read -hu; and aʿṭā takes li- for the one given to, again Middle Arabic. lā tuwākhidhīnī, “do not hold it against me”, is a set phrase of apology, Classical lā tuʾākhidhīnī (jussive tuʾākhidhī + -nī, “me”). The print's spelling with wāw (توأخذينى) reflects the spoken form tuwākhidh-.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَ عَزِيزًا أَنْ يَدْفَعَ لَهَا أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-amara ʿazīzan an yadfaʿa lahā alfa dīnārin
sentences.l: And he ordered ʿAzīz that he pay to her a thousand dinars.
sentences.i: And he told ʿAzīz to pay her a thousand dinars.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا أُمِّي إِنَّ هَذِةِ الْوَرَقَةَ لَابُدَّ أَنْ يَعْقُبَهَا كَمَالُ الِاتِّصَالِ أَوْ كَمَالُ الِانْفِصَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā yā ummī inna hādhihi al-waraqata lā budda an yaʿqubahā kamālu al-ittiṣāli aw kamālu al-infiṣāli
sentences.l: And he said to her: O my mother, indeed this paper, there is no escape (but) that there follow it the completeness of the joining or the completeness of the parting.
sentences.i: And he said to her, “Mother, this letter must be followed either by our union in full or by our parting for good.”
sentences.n: yā ummī, “my mother”: a polite address to an old woman. The pair al-ittiṣāl / al-infiṣāl, “union / separation”, rhymes. The print spells hādhihi as هذة and runs lā budda together (لابد).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي وَاللَّهِ مَا أَشْتَهِي لَكَ إِلَّا الْخَيْرَ وَمُرَادِي أَنْ تَكُونَ هِيَ عِنْدَكَ فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْقَمَرُ صَاحِبُ الْأَنْوَارِ السَّاطِعَةِ وَهِيَ الشَّمْسُ الطَّالِعَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu yā waladī wa-allāhi mā ashtahī laka illā al-khayra wa-murādī an takūna hiya ʿindaka fa-innaka anta al-qamaru ṣāḥibu al-anwāri al-sāṭiʿati wa-hiya al-shamsu al-ṭāliʿatu
sentences.l: And she said to him: O my son, by God, I do not desire for you except the good, and my wish (is) that she be with you; for you, you (are) the moon, owner of the lights the radiant, and she (is) the sun the rising.
sentences.i: She said to him, “My son, by God, I want nothing for you but good, and my wish is that she should be yours; for you are the moon with its radiant light, and she is the rising sun.”
sentences.n: The rhyme falls on al-sāṭiʿa / al-ṭāliʿa. ʿindaka, “with you”: hers, in his keeping.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ لَمْ أَجْمَعْ بَيْنَكُمَا فَلَيْسَ فِى حَيَوٰتِي فَائِدَةٌ وَأَنَا قَدْ قَطَعْتُ عُمْرِي فِي الْمَكْرِ وَالْخِدَاعِ حَتَّى بَلَغْتُ التِّسْعِينَ مِنَ الْأَعْوَامِ فَكَيْفَ أَعْجِزُ عَنِ الْجَمْعِ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ فِى الْحَرَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-in lam ajmaʿ baynakumā fa-laysa fī ḥayātī fāʾidatun wa-anā qad qaṭaʿtu ʿumrī fī al-makri wa-al-khidāʿi ḥattā balaghtu al-tisʿīna mina al-aʿwāmi fa-kayfa aʿjizu ʿani al-jamʿi bayna ithnayni fī al-ḥarāmi
sentences.l: And if I do not bring-together between you two, then there is not in my life (any) use; and I have spent my lifetime in the cunning and the deceit until I reached the ninety of the years — so how should I be incapable of the bringing-together between two in the forbidden?
sentences.i: If I do not bring the two of you together, my life is good for nothing. I have spent my whole life in cunning and trickery, till I have reached ninety years — so how could I fail to bring two people together in sin?
sentences.n: The print spells ḥayātī, “my life”, with wāw (حيوتي), the old spelling of ḥayāt; the small alif over the wāw is ours. fī al-ḥarām, “in the forbidden”: in an unlawful union, and she says so without embarrassment. The rhyme falls on al-khidāʿ … al-aʿwām … al-ḥarām. The print spells fī with a final ى (فى) twice here.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَدَّعَتْهُ وَطَيَّبَتْ قَلْبَهُ وَانْصَرَفَتْ وَلَمْ تَزَلْ تَمْشِي حَتَّى دَخَلَتْ عَلَى السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا وَقَدْ أَخْفَتِ الْوَرَقَةَ فِي شَعْرِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma waddaʿathu wa-ṭayyabat qalbahu wa-inṣarafat wa-lam tazal tamshī ḥattā dakhalat ʿalā al-sayyidati dunyā wa-qad akhfati al-waraqata fī shaʿrihā
sentences.l: Then she bade him farewell and made-good his heart and departed, and she did not cease walking until she entered upon the Lady Dunyā, and she had hidden the paper in her hair.
sentences.i: Then she said goodbye to him, cheered his heart and went away, and walked on until she came in to the Lady Dunyā, with the letter hidden in her hair.
sentences.n: ṭayyaba qalbahu, “to make someone's heart good”: to reassure, to comfort. The print marks the doubled letters of waddaʿathu and ṭayyabat (ودّعته، وطيّبت).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَلَسَتْ عِنْدَهَا حَلَّتْ رَأْسَهَا وَقَالَتْ يَاسَيِّدَتِي عَسَاكِ أَنْ تَفْلِي شُوشَتِي فَإِنَّ لِي زَمَانًا مَادَخَلْتُ الْحَمَّامَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jalasat ʿindahā ḥallat raʾsahā wa-qālat yā sayyidatī ʿasāki an taflī shūshatī fa-inna lī zamānan mā dakhaltu al-ḥammāma
sentences.l: And when she sat with her, she untied her head and said: O my lady, perhaps you (would) delouse my hair-tuft, for indeed to me (is) a time (that) I have not entered the bath.
sentences.i: When she had sat down with her, she let down her hair and said, “My lady, would you pick the lice from my hair? It is a long time since I last went to the baths.”
sentences.n: ḥallat raʾsahā, “she untied her head”: she let down her hair, where she has hidden the letter. ʿasāki an, “perhaps you (would)”, a polite request. falā, yaflī, “to pick lice from”. shūsha, “tuft of hair, topknot”, is a colloquial word. The print runs yā sayyidatī and mā dakhaltu together (ياسيدتي، مادخلت).

sentences.t: فَكَشَفَتِ السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا عَنْ مِرْفَقَيْهَا وَحَلَّتْ شَعْرَ الْعَجُوزِ وَصَارَتْ تَفْلِي شُوشَهَا فَسَقَطَتِ الْوَرَقَةُ مِنْ رَأْسِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-kashafati al-sayyidatu dunyā ʿan mirfaqayhā wa-ḥallat shaʿra al-ʿajūzi wa-ṣārat taflī shūshahā fa-saqaṭati al-waraqatu min raʾsihā
sentences.l: And the Lady Dunyā uncovered (from) her two elbows, and untied the hair of the old woman, and began delousing her hair-tuft; and the paper fell from her head.
sentences.i: The Lady Dunyā pushed her sleeves back from her elbows, loosened the old woman's hair and set to picking the lice from it; and the paper fell out of her hair.
sentences.n: kashafat ʿan mirfaqayhā, “she uncovered her two elbows”: she pushed back her sleeves. shūshahā, “her tuft”, is printed without the -at- of shūshatī just before (شوشها); it may be a slip for shūshatahā or another form of the word, and is kept as printed. ṣārat tafʿalu, “she began to do”.

sentences.t: فَرَأَتْهَا السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا فَقَالَتْ مَا هَذِهِ الْوَرَقَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾathā al-sayyidatu dunyā fa-qālat mā hādhihi al-waraqatu
sentences.l: And the Lady Dunyā saw it, and said: What (is) this paper?
sentences.i: The Lady Dunyā saw it and said, “What is this paper?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ كَأَنِّي قَعَدْتُ عَلَى دُكَّانِ التَّاجِرِ فَتَعَلَّقَتْ مَعِى هَذِهِ الْوَرَقَةُ هَا تِيهَا حَتَّى أُوَدِّيهَا لَهُ رُبَّمَا يَكُونُ فِيهَا حِسَابٌ يَحْتَاجُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ka-annī qaʿadtu ʿalā dukkāni al-tājiri fa-taʿallaqat maʿī hādhihi al-waraqatu hātīhā ḥattā uwaddīhā lahu rubbamā yakūnu fīhā ḥisābun yaḥtājuhu
sentences.l: And she said: As-if I sat at the shop of the merchant, and this paper clung with me. Give-it-here, so that I take it to him; perhaps there is in it an account (that) he needs.
sentences.i: She said, “I must have sat down at the merchant's shop, and this paper caught on me. Give it here, and I will take it back to him; there may be some account in it that he needs.”
sentences.n: The print sets hātīhā, “give it here” (the feminine of the imperative hāt, “give!”, with -hā, “it”), as two words, ها تيها; the spacing is kept. ka-annī, “as if I”, here “it seems I”. taʿallaqat maʿī, “it clung with me”: it got caught on me. uwaddīhā, “I take it”, from colloquial waddā, “to take, to convey”; it could also be read uʾaddīhā, “I deliver it”, with the hamza unwritten. The print spells maʿī with a final ى (معى) and marks the kasra of al-tājiri.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَتْهَا السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا وَقَرَأَتْهَا وَفَهِمَتْ مَا فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥathā al-sayyidatu dunyā wa-qaraʾathā wa-fahimat mā fīhā
sentences.l: And the Lady Dunyā opened it and read it and understood what (was) in it.
sentences.i: The Lady Dunyā opened it, read it and understood what it said.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِلْعَجُوزِ هَذِهِ حِيلَةٌ مِنْ بَعْضِ حِيَلِكِ وَلَوْلَا أَنَّكِ رَبَّيْتِنِي لَبَطَشْتُ بِكِ فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat li-al-ʿajūzi hādhihi ḥīlatun min baʿḍi ḥiyaliki wa-lawlā annaki rabbaytinī la-baṭashtu biki fī hādhā al-waqti
sentences.l: And she said to the old woman: This (is) a trick from some of your tricks; and were-it-not that you raised me, I would have struck-at you in this time.
sentences.i: And she said to the old woman, “This is one of your tricks! If you had not brought me up, I would fall on you this very moment.”
sentences.n: baṭasha bi-, “to seize violently, to strike at”: the verb takes bi-. lawlā anna … la-, “were it not that … then”: la- marks the consequence. The print marks the kasra of biki, “you” (feminine).

sentences.t: وَقَدْ بَلَانِي اللَّهُ بِهَذَا التَّاجِرِ وَكُلُّ مَاجَرَى لِي مِنْهُ مِنْ تَحْتِ رَأْسِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad balānī allāhu bi-hādhā al-tājiri wa-kullu mā jarā lī minhu min taḥti raʾsiki
sentences.l: And God has afflicted me with this merchant, and all-that has happened to me from him (is) from under your head.
sentences.i: God has afflicted me with this merchant, and everything I have had to bear from him is your doing.
sentences.n: balā bi-, “to try, to afflict with”: bi- marks the affliction. min taḥti raʾsiki, “from under your head”: your work, your doing. The print runs mā jarā together (ماجرى).

sentences.t: وَمَا أَدْرِي مِنْ أَيِّ أَرْضٍ جَاءَنَا هَذَا وَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ أَحَدٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ أَنْ يَتَجَاسَرَ عَلَيَّ غَيْرُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-mā adrī min ayyi arḍin jāʾanā hādhā wa-lam yaqdir aḥadun mina al-nāsi an yatajāsara ʿalayya ghayruhu
sentences.l: And I do not know from which land this (one) came to us; and not was anyone of the people able to dare upon me, other-than-him.
sentences.i: I do not know what land this man has come to us from; no one but he has ever dared to take such liberties with me.
sentences.n: tajāsara ʿalā, “to make bold with, to presume upon”. lam yaqdir … an, “was not able to”, here simply “no one has dared”.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَخَافُ أَنْ يَنْكَشِفَ أَمْرِي وَخُصُوصًا فِي رَجُلٍ مَاهُوَ مِنْ جِنْسِي وَلَا مِنْ أَقْرَانِي
sentences.tr: wa-anā akhāfu an yankashifa amrī wa-khuṣūṣan fī rajulin mā huwa min jinsī wa-lā min aqrānī
sentences.l: And I fear that my affair be uncovered, and especially in (the matter of) a man (who) is not of my kind and not of my peers.
sentences.i: And I am afraid my secret will come out — above all when it concerns a man who is not of my rank, nor my equal.
sentences.n: mā huwa, “he is not”, for Classical laysa, is run together in the print (ماهو). fī, “in”, here “in the matter of, concerning”.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَتِ الْعَجُوزُ عَلَيْهَا وَقَالَتْ لَا يَقْدِرُ أَحَدٌ أَنْ يَتَكَلَّمَ بِهَذَا الْكَلَامِ خَوْفًا مِنْ سَطْوَتِكِ وَهَيْبَةِ أَبِيكِ وَلَابَأْسَ أَنْ تَرُدِّي لَهُ الْجَوَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbalati al-ʿajūzu ʿalayhā wa-qālat lā yaqdiru aḥadun an yatakallama bi-hādhā al-kalāmi khawfan min saṭwatiki wa-haybati abīki wa-lā baʾsa an turuddī lahu al-jawāba
sentences.l: And the old woman turned toward her and said: No one is able to speak with this speech, (out of) fear of your might and the awe of your father; and (there is) no harm that you return to him the answer.
sentences.i: The old woman turned to her and said, “No one would dare breathe a word of this, for fear of your power and the awe your father inspires. And there is no harm in your sending him an answer.”
sentences.n: aqbala ʿalā, “to turn to, to face”. takallama bi-, “to speak (words)”: bi- marks what is said. lā baʾsa, “no harm”, is run together in the print and written without its hamza (ولاباس). radda lahu al-jawāb, “to return him the answer”: to write back.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا دَادَتِى إِنَّ هَذَا شَيْطَانٌ كَيْفَ تَجَاسَرَ عَلَى هَذَا الْكَلَامِ وَلَمْ يَخَفْ مِنْ سَطْوَةِ السُّلْطَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā dādatī inna hādhā shayṭānun kayfa tajāsara ʿalā hādhā al-kalāmi wa-lam yakhaf min saṭwati al-sulṭāni
sentences.l: And she said: O my nurse, indeed this (one is) a devil! How did he dare upon this speech, and did not fear the might of the sultan?
sentences.i: She said, “Nanny, this man is a devil! How did he dare to say such things, with no fear of the Sultan's power?”
sentences.n: dāda, “nurse, nanny”, is a word from Persian; the print spells dādatī with a final ى (دادتى). shayṭān and sulṭān rhyme. The sultan is her father, King Shahramān.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ تَحَيَّرْتُ فِى أَمْرِهِ فَإِنْ أَمَرْتُ بِقَتْلِهِ فَلَيْسَ بِصَوَابٍ وَإِنْ تَرَكْتُهُ ازْدَادَ فِي تَجَاسُرِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad taḥayyartu fī amrihi fa-in amartu bi-qatlihi fa-laysa bi-ṣawābin wa-in taraktuhu izdāda fī tajāsurihi
sentences.l: And I have become-perplexed in his affair: for if I order his killing, it is not right; and if I leave him, he increases in his daring.
sentences.i: I do not know what to do about him: to have him killed would not be right, and if I leave him alone he will only grow bolder.
sentences.n: amara bi-, “to order”: bi- marks what is ordered. laysa bi-ṣawābin, “it is not right”: bi- after a negative only strengthens it. The print spells fī with a final ى (فى) and marks the kasra of tajāsurihi.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا الْعَجُوزُ اكْتُبِي لَهُ كِتَابًا لَعَلَّهُ يَنْزَجِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā al-ʿajūzu uktubī lahu kitāban laʿallahu yanzajiru
sentences.l: And the old woman said to her: Write to him a letter; perhaps he will be-restrained.
sentences.i: The old woman said to her, “Write him a letter; perhaps that will check him.”
sentences.n: inzajara, “to be checked, to desist”.

sentences.t: فَطَلَبَتْ وَرَقَةً وَدَوَاةً وَقَلَمًا وَكَتَبَتْ لَهُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalabat waraqatan wa-dawātan wa-qalaman wa-katabat lahu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And she asked for paper and an inkwell and a pen, and wrote to him these verses:
sentences.i: So she called for paper, inkwell and pen, and wrote him these verses:

sentences.t:
طَالَ الْعِتَابُ وَفَرْطُ الْجَهْلِ اَغْرَاكَا * فَكَمْ بِخَطِّ يَدِىْ فِى الشِّعْرِ اَنْهَاكَا
وَاَنْتَ تَزْدَادُ عِنْدَ النَّهْيِ فِي طَمَعٍ * وَلَسْتُ الَّا بِكَتْمِ السِّرِّ اَرْضَاكَا
اُكْتُمْ هَوَاكَ وَلَا تَجْهَرْ بِهِ اَبَدًا * وَاِنْ نَطَقْتَ فَاِنِّي لَسْتُ اِرْعَاكَا
وَاِنْ رَجَعْتَ اِلَى مَا اَنْتَ تَذْكُرُهُ * فَقَدْ اَتَاكَ غُرَابُ الْبَيْنِ يَنْعَاكَا
وَعَنْ قَلِيلٍ يَكُونُ الْمَوْتُ مُنْدَفِعاً * عَلَيْكَ وَالدَّفْنُ تَحْتَ الْاَرْضِ مَثْوَاكَا
وَتَتْرُكُ الْاَهْلَ يَا مَغْرُوْرُ فِي نَدَمٍ * عَلَى فِرَاقِكَ طُوْلَ الدَّهْرِ يَنْعَاكَا
sentences.tr:
ṭāla al-ʿitābu wa-farṭu al-jahli aghrāka * fa-kam bi-khaṭṭi yadī fī al-shiʿri anhāka
wa-anta tazdādu ʿinda al-nahyi fī ṭamaʿin * wa-lastu illā bi-katmi al-sirri arḍāka
uktum hawāka wa-lā tajhar bihi abadan * wa-in naṭaqta fa-innī lastu irʿāka
wa-in rajaʿta ilā mā anta tadhkuruhu * fa-qad atāka ghurābu al-bayni yanʿāka
wa-ʿan qalīlin yakūnu al-mawtu mundafiʿan * ʿalayka wa-al-dafnu taḥta al-arḍi mathwāka
wa-tatruku al-ahla yā maghrūru fī nadamin * ʿalā firāqika ṭūla al-dahri yanʿāka
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. The print points irʿāka, “I regard you”, with a kasra on the alif (اِرْعَاكَا), where arʿāka is expected; the print's vowel is kept. bi-katmi al-sirri, “with the keeping of the secret”: bi- of condition, “only on condition that you keep it secret”. ghurāb al-bayn, “the raven of parting”, is the bird whose cry foretells separation and death; naʿā, “to announce a death”, gives yanʿāka, “announcing your death”, which the poem uses twice as its rhyme word, the second time with al-ahl, “the family”, as its subject. mundafiʿan is printed with its tanwīn sign before the alif (مُنْدَفِعاً). Dunyā again addresses him in the masculine singular, and this time she leaves him a door open: secrecy.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَوَتِ الْوَرَقَةَ وَدَفَعَتْهَا لِلْعَجُوزِ فَأَخَذَتْهَا وَتَوَجَّهَتْ إِلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ فَأَعْطَتْهَا لَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭawati al-waraqata wa-dafaʿathā li-al-ʿajūzi fa-akhadhathā wa-tawajjahat ilā tāji al-mulūki fa-aʿṭathā lahu
sentences.l: Then she folded the paper and handed it to the old woman; and she took it and headed to Tāj al-Mulūk, and gave it to him.
sentences.i: Then she folded the paper and handed it to the old woman, who took it to Tāj al-Mulūk and gave it to him.
sentences.n: dafaʿahā li-, “to hand it to”: li- marks the one who receives it, where Classical prefers ilā. aʿṭathā lahu, “she gave it to him”, with li- for the receiver, is Middle Arabic for Classical aʿṭathu iyyāhā.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرَأَهَا عَلِمَ أَنَّهَا قَاسِيَةُ الْقَلْبِ وَأَنَّهُ لَا يَصِلُ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaraʾahā ʿalima annahā qāsiyatu al-qalbi wa-annahu lā yaṣilu ilayhā
sentences.l: And when he read it, he knew that she (was) hard of the heart, and that he would not reach to her.
sentences.i: When he read it he knew that she was hard-hearted, and that he would never win her.

sentences.t: فَشَكَا أَمْرَهُ إِلَى الْوَزِيرِ وَطَلَبَ مِنْهُ حُسْنَ التَّدْبِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-shakā amrahu ilā al-wazīri wa-ṭalaba minhu ḥusna al-tadbīri
sentences.l: And he complained (of) his affair to the vizier, and sought from him goodness of the planning.
sentences.i: So he laid his trouble before the vizier and asked him for sound counsel.
sentences.n: al-wazīr and al-tadbīr rhyme. This is the prince's own vizier, who came with him in disguise.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ اعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ مَا بَقِيَ شَيْءٌ يُفِيدُ فِيهَا غَيْرَ أَنَّكَ تَكْتُبُ لَهَا كِتَابًا وَتَدْعُو عَلَيْهَا فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru iʿlam annahu mā baqiya shayʾun yufīdu fīhā ghayra annaka taktubu lahā kitāban wa-tadʿū ʿalayhā fīhi
sentences.l: And the vizier said to him: Know that there has not remained a thing (that) avails in her, other than that you write to her a letter and pray against her in it.
sentences.i: The vizier said to him, “You must understand that nothing is left that will work with her, except for you to write her a letter and call down curses on her in it.”
sentences.n: daʿā ʿalā, “to pray against, to curse”; daʿā li- would be “to pray for”. afāda fī, “to avail with, to have an effect on”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا أَخِي يَا عَزِيزُ اكْتُبْ لَهَا عَنْ لِسَانِي مِثْلَ مَا تَعْرِفُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā akhī yā ʿazīzu uktub lahā ʿan lisānī mithla mā taʿrifu
sentences.l: And he said: O my brother, O ʿAzīz, write to her on-behalf-of my tongue, like what you know.
sentences.i: He said, “Brother ʿAzīz, write to her for me, as you know how.”
sentences.n: ʿan lisānī, “from my tongue”: in my name, as though I were speaking.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ عَزِيزٌ وَرَقَةً وَكَتَبَ هَذِةِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha ʿazīzun waraqatan wa-kataba hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And ʿAzīz took a paper and wrote these verses:
sentences.i: So ʿAzīz took a sheet of paper and wrote these verses:
sentences.n: The print spells hādhihi with a final tāʾ marbūṭa (هذة).

sentences.t:
يَا رَبِّ بِالْخَمْسَةِ الْاَشْبَاحِ تُنْقِذُنِي * وَمَنْ بُلِيتُ بِهِ فَاجْعَلْهُ فِي شَجَنِي
فَاَنْتَ تَعْلَمُ اَنِّي فِي جَوًى لَهَبٍ * وَقَدْ جَفَانِي حَبِيبٌ لَيْسَ يَرْحَمُنِي
فَكَمْ اَرِقُّ لَهَا فِيمَا بُلِيتُ بِهِ * وَكَمْ تَجُوْرُ عَلَى ضَعْفِي وَتَظْلِمُنِي
اَهِيمُ فِي غَمَرَاتٍ لَا انْقِضَاءَ لَهَا * وَلَا اَرَى مُسْعِفًا يَارَبِّ يُسْعِفُنِي
وَكَمْ اَرُوْمُ سُلُوًّا فِي مَحَبَّتِهَا * وَكَيْفَ اَسْلُو وَصَبْرِي فِي الْغَرَامِ فَنِي
يَا مَانِعِي فِي الْهَوَى طِيبَ الْوِصَالِ فَهَلْ * اَمِنْتَ مِنْ نَائِبَاتِ الدَّهْرِ وَالْمِحَنِ
اَلَسْتِ فِي عِيشَةٍ مَسْرُوْرَةٍ وَاَنَا * مُغَرَّبٌ فِيكِ عَنْ اَهْلِي وَعَنْ وَطَنِي
sentences.tr:
yā rabbi bi-al-khamsati al-ashbāḥi tunqidhunī * wa-man bulītu bihi fa-jʿalhu fī shajanī
fa-anta taʿlamu annī fī jawan lahabin * wa-qad jafānī ḥabībun laysa yarḥamunī
fa-kam ariqqu lahā fīmā bulītu bihi * wa-kam tajūru ʿalā ḍaʿfī wa-taẓlimunī
ahīmu fī ghamarātin lā inqiḍāʾa lahā * wa-lā arā musʿifan yā rabbi yusʿifunī
wa-kam arūmu suluwwan fī maḥabbatihā * wa-kayfa aslū wa-ṣabrī fī al-gharāmi fanī
yā māniʿī fī al-hawā ṭība al-wiṣāli fa-hal * aminta min nāʾibāti al-dahri wa-al-miḥani
a-lasti fī ʿīshatin masrūratin wa-anā * mugharrabun fīki ʿan ahlī wa-ʿan waṭanī
sentences.l:
O Lord, by the five figures, (may) You rescue me; * and (the one) whom I have been afflicted with, put him in my grief!
For You know that I (am) in a passion, a flame, * and a beloved has shunned me (who) is not having-mercy on me.
So how often I grow-tender toward her in what I have been afflicted with, * and how often she tyrannizes over my weakness and wrongs me!
I wander-distraught in floods (that have) no ending to them, * and I do not see a helper, O Lord, (who) helps me.
And how often I seek consolation in her love — * and how (can) I be consoled, when my patience in the passion has perished?
O withholder from me, in the love, of the sweetness of the union: so are * you safe from the calamities of the time and the trials?
Are you not in a life gladdened, while I * (am) made-a-stranger in you, from my family and from my homeland?
sentences.i:
O Lord, by the Five Holy Ones, deliver me, * and bring the one who torments me into my own sorrow!
You know that I burn in a flame of passion, * and a beloved shuns me who will not pity me.
How often I have softened toward her in all I suffer, * and how often she tramples my weakness and does me wrong!
I wander lost in floods that have no ending, * and I see no helper, Lord, to help me.
How often I try to cure myself of loving her — * but how can I forget, when my patience in love is spent?
You who deny me, in love, the sweetness of union: * do you think yourself safe from the blows of fate and its trials?
Are you not living in delight, while I * am an exile for your sake, far from my people and my home?
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. al-khamsa al-ashbāḥ, “the five figures”, are Muḥammad, ʿAlī, Fāṭima, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, the People of the Cloak, by whom Shīʿī prayers swear; the number stands before its noun, both with the article. tunqidhunī, “You rescue me”, is a plain present used as a prayer. bulītu bihi, “I have been afflicted with”: bi- marks the affliction. fī jawan lahabin, “in a passion, a flame”: the second noun stands beside the first to describe it. fanī is faniya, “has perished”, in its rhyme form. ʿīsha, “life”, is printed with yāʾ (عِيشَة). mugharrabun fīki, “made a stranger in you”: fī of cause, “for your sake”. The beloved is spoken of as “her”, then addressed in the masculine (yā māniʿī, aminta), and in the last line in the feminine (a-lasti). The curse the vizier asked for is mild: that she be made to share his grief.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَزِيزًا طَوَى الْكِتَابَ وَنَاوَلَهُ لِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ فَلَمَّا قَرَأَهُ أَعْجَبَهُ ثُمَّ نَاوَلَهُ لِلْعَجُوزِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna ʿazīzan ṭawā al-kitāba wa-nāwalahu li-tāji al-mulūki fa-lammā qaraʾahu aʿjabahu thumma nāwalahu li-al-ʿajūzi
sentences.l: Then ʿAzīz folded the letter and handed it to Tāj al-Mulūk; and when he read it, it pleased him; then he handed it to the old woman.
sentences.i: Then ʿAzīz folded the letter and handed it to Tāj al-Mulūk, who read it and was pleased with it, and then handed it to the old woman.
sentences.n: thumma inna, “then (indeed)”: the narrator's way of moving the story on. nāwala, “to hand”, takes its object directly in Classical Arabic (nāwalahu iyyāhu); here the one handed to is marked with li-, “to”, a Middle Arabic habit.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْهُ الْعَجُوزُ وَتَوَجَّهَتْ بِهِ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلَتْ عَلَي السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا فَنَاوَلَتْهَا إِيَّاةُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhathu al-ʿajūzu wa-tawajjahat bihi ilā an dakhalat ʿalā al-sayyidati dunyā fa-nāwalathā iyyāhu
sentences.l: And the old woman took it and set-out with it until that she entered upon the Lady Dunyā, and she handed her it.
sentences.i: The old woman took it and set off with it until she came in to the Lady Dunyā, and gave it to her.
sentences.n: tawajjahat bihi, “she headed off with it”: bi- of what is carried along. ilā an, “until”. dakhala ʿalā, “to go in to (someone)”; the print spells ʿalā with a dotted yāʾ (علي), read ʿalā. The print spells iyyāhu, “it”, with a final ة (اياة), as it does hādhihi (هذة); read -hu.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرَأَتْهَا وَفَهِمَتْ مَضْمُونَهُ اغْتَاظَتْ غَيْظًا شَدِيدًا وَقَالَتْ كُلُّ الَّذِي جَرَي لِي مِنْ تَحْتِ رَأْسِ هَذِةِ الْعَجُوزِ النَّحْسِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaraʾathā wa-fahimat maḍmūnahu ightāẓat ghayẓan shadīdan wa-qālat kullu alladhī jarā lī min taḥti raʾsi hādhihi al-ʿajūzi al-naḥsi
sentences.l: And when she read it and understood its contents, she raged a rage violent, and said: All that which happened to me (is) from under the head of this old-woman, the ill-omened!
sentences.i: When she had read it and taken in what it said, she flew into a violent rage and said, “Everything that has happened to me is the doing of this ill-omened old woman!”
sentences.n: qaraʾathā, “she read it”, with a feminine “it”, as if for risāla, “letter”, though the next word, maḍmūnahu, “its contents”, goes back to the masculine kitāb. min taḥti raʾsi, “from under the head of”: colloquial for “all the work of, all because of”. The print spells jarā with a dotted yāʾ (جري) and raʾs without its hamza (راس). al-naḥs, “ill-luck”, used as an adjective: “the jinx”.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَتْ عَلَي الْجَوَارِي وَالْخَدَمِ وَقَالَتْ أَمْسِكُوا هَذِةِ الْعَجُوزَ الْمَلْعُونَةَ الْمَاكِرَةَ وَاضْرِبُوهَا بِنِعَالِكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥat ʿalā al-jawārī wa-al-khadami wa-qālat amsikū hādhihi al-ʿajūza al-malʿūnata al-mākirata wa-iḍribūhā bi-niʿālikum
sentences.l: And she shouted at the slave-girls and the servants and said: Seize this old-woman, the accursed, the crafty, and beat her with your sandals!
sentences.i: She shouted for her slave-girls and servants and said, “Seize this damned, crafty old woman and beat her with your sandals!”
sentences.n: ṣāḥa ʿalā, “to shout at, to call (servants)”; ʿalā is again printed علي. bi-niʿālikum, “with your sandals”: bi- of the instrument. A beating with shoes is a beating meant to shame.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلُوا عَلَيْهَا ضَرْبًا بِالنِّعَالِ حَتَّى غُشِيَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-nazalū ʿalayhā ḍarban bi-al-niʿāli ḥattā ghushiya ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And they came-down upon her (with) beating with the sandals until it was swooned upon her.
sentences.i: They fell on her, beating her with their sandals, until she fainted.
sentences.n: nazala ʿalā … ḍarban, “to come down on someone with blows”, to set about them. ghushiya ʿalayhā, “she fainted”, literally “(a covering) was laid over her”: an impersonal passive.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَتْ قَالَتْ لَهَا وَاللَّهِ يَا عَجُوزَ السُّوءِ لَوْ لَاخَوْفِى مِنَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى لَقَتَلْتُكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqat qālat lahā wa-allāhi yā ʿajūza al-sūʾi lawlā khawfī mina allāhi taʿālā la-qataltuki
sentences.l: And when she came-to, she said to her: By God, O old-woman of the evil, were it not for my fear of God the Exalted, I would have killed you!
sentences.i: When she came round, Dunyā said to her, “By God, you wicked old woman, if it were not for my fear of God Most High, I would have killed you!”
sentences.n: The print has لتنلتك, a misprint for لقتلتك, la-qataltuki, “I would have killed you”, corrected here. lawlā, “were it not for”, is set by the print with odd spacing, لو لاخوفى, the lā run onto khawfī instead of onto law; it is the one word lawlā all the same. The print spells khawfī with a final ى. ʿajūz al-sūʾ, “old woman of evil”, “wicked old woman”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُمْ أَعِيدُوا عَلَيْهَا الضَّرْبَ فَضَرَبُوهَا حَتَّى غُشِيَ عَلَيْهَا ثُمَّ أَمَرَتْهُمْ أَنْ يَجُرُّوهَا وَيَرْمُوهَا خَارِجَ الْبَابِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahum aʿīdū ʿalayhā al-ḍarba fa-ḍarabūhā ḥattā ghushiya ʿalayhā thumma amarathum an yajurrūhā wa-yarmūhā khārija al-bābi
sentences.l: Then she said to them: Repeat upon her the beating! And they beat her until it was swooned upon her; then she ordered them that they drag her and throw her outside the door.
sentences.i: Then she said to them, “Beat her again!” They beat her until she fainted, and then she ordered them to drag her off and throw her out of the door.
sentences.n: aʿāda ʿalā, “to repeat on (someone)”. The doubling mark on يجرّوها, yajurrūhā, “they drag her”, is the print's.

sentences.t: فَسَحَبُوهَا عَلَى وَجْهِهَا وَرَمَوْهَا قُدَّامَ الْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-saḥabūhā ʿalā wajhihā wa-ramawhā quddāma al-bābi
sentences.l: And they dragged her on her face and threw her in front of the door.
sentences.i: So they dragged her along on her face and flung her down outside the door.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَتْ قَامَتْ تَمْشِي وَتَقْعُدُ حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهَا وَصَبَرَتْ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqat qāmat tamshī wa-taqʿudu ḥattā waṣalat ilā manzilihā wa-ṣabarat ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And when she came-to, she rose, walking and sitting, until she reached her dwelling, and she endured until the morning.
sentences.i: When she came round she got up and went on, walking a little and sitting a little, until she reached her house, and there she bore it until morning.
sentences.n: qāmat tamshī wa-taqʿudu, “she got up, walking and sitting”: she had to stop and rest again and again.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَتْ وَتَمَشَّتْ حَتَّى أَتَتْ إِلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَأَخْبَرَتْهُ بِجَمِيعِ مَا جَرَى لَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma qāmat wa-tamashshat ḥattā atat ilā tāji al-mulūki wa-akhbarathu bi-jamīʿi mā jarā lahā
sentences.l: Then she rose and walked-along until she came to Tāj al-Mulūk and informed him of all that happened to her.
sentences.i: Then she got up and made her way to Tāj al-Mulūk, and told him all that had happened to her.
sentences.n: The doubling mark on تمشّت, tamashshat, “she walked along”, is the print's. akhbara bi-, “to tell of”: the verb takes bi-.

sentences.t: فَصَعُبَ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ لَهَا يَعِزُّ عَلَيْنَا يَا أُمِّي مَا جَرَى لَكِ وَلَكِنْ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ بِقَضَاءٍ وَقَدَرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣaʿuba ʿalayhi dhālika wa-qāla lahā yaʿizzu ʿalaynā yā ummī mā jarā laki wa-lākin kullu shayʾin bi-qaḍāʾin wa-qadarin
sentences.l: And that was hard upon him, and he said to her: It is grievous upon us, O my mother, what happened to you; but every thing (is) by decree and destiny.
sentences.i: It weighed on him, and he said to her, “It grieves me, mother, what has happened to you; but everything comes by God's decree and destiny.”
sentences.n: yaʿizzu ʿalaynā, “it is hard on us, it pains us”; the doubling mark is the print's. yā ummī, “O my mother”, is a courtesy to an old woman. bi-qaḍāʾin wa-qadar: bi-, “by”, of the cause.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ طِبْ نَفْسًا وَقَرَّ عَيْنًا فَإِنِّي لَا أَزَالُ أَسْعَي حَتَّى أَجْمَعَ بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهَا وَأُوصِلَكَ إِلَى هَذِةِ الْعَاهِرَةِ الَّتِي أَحْرَقَتْنِي بِالضَّرْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan fa-innī lā azālu asʿā ḥattā ajmaʿa baynaka wa-baynahā wa-ūṣilaka ilā hādhihi al-ʿāhirati allatī aḥraqatnī bi-al-ḍarbi
sentences.l: And she said to him: Be good of soul and be cool of eye, for I do not cease striving until I join between you and her, and bring you to this whore who burned me with the beating.
sentences.i: She said to him, “Cheer up and be easy, for I will not rest until I bring you and her together and get you to this whore who has set me on fire with her beating.”
sentences.n: ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan, “be good of soul and cool of eye”: a stock pair meaning “take heart, be content”; the doubling mark on qarra is the print's. The print spells asʿā, “I strive”, with a dotted yāʾ (اسعي). jamaʿa bayna … wa-bayna, “to bring … and … together”. The old woman's ʿāhira, “whore”, is plain abuse, and the text means it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ أَخْبِرِينِي مَا سَبَبُ بُغْضِهَا لِلرِّجَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā tāju al-mulūki akhbirīnī mā sababu bughḍihā li-al-rijāli
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk said to her: Inform me, what (is) the cause of her hatred for the men?
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk said to her, “Tell me, why does she hate men?”
sentences.n: bughḍuhā li-al-rijāl, “her hatred for men”: li- marks the object of the feeling.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِأَنَّهَا رَأَتْ مَنَامًا أَوْجَبَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat li-annahā raʾat manāman awjaba dhālika
sentences.l: And she said: Because she saw a dream (that) necessitated that.
sentences.i: She said, “Because she had a dream that brought it about.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا وَمَا ذَلِكَ الْمَنَامُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā wa-mā dhālika al-manāmu
sentences.l: And he said to her: And what (is) that dream?
sentences.i: He said to her, “And what was that dream?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ نَائِمَةً ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ فَرَأَتْ صَيَّادًا نَصَبَ شَرَكًا فِى الْأَرْضِ وَبَذَرَ حَوْلَهُ قَمْحًا ثُمَّ جَلَسَ قَرِيبًا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat innahā kānat nāʾimatan dhāta laylatin fa-raʾat ṣayyādan naṣaba sharakan fī al-arḍi wa-badhara ḥawlahu qamḥan thumma jalasa qarīban minhu
sentences.l: And she said: She was sleeping one night, and she saw a fowler (who) set a snare in the ground and scattered around it wheat; then he sat near to it.
sentences.i: She said, “She was asleep one night, and she dreamed she saw a fowler set a net on the ground and scatter wheat around it, and then sit down close by.
sentences.n: ṣayyād, “hunter”, here a bird-catcher; the doubling mark on صيّادا is the print's. sharak, “snare, net”. dhāta laylatin, “one night”. The print spells fī with a final ى (فى) throughout this passage.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَبْقَ شَيْءٌ مِنَ الطُّيُورِ إِلَّا وَقَدْ أَتَى إِلَى ذَلِكَ الشَّرَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yabqa shayʾun mina al-ṭuyūri illā wa-qad atā ilā dhālika al-sharaki
sentences.l: And there did not remain a thing of the birds except (that) it had come to that snare.
sentences.i: Not one of the birds was left that had not come to the net.

sentences.t: وَرَأَتْ فِى الطُّيُورِ حَمَامَتَيْنِ ذَكَرًا وَأُنْثَى
sentences.tr: wa-raʾat fī al-ṭuyūri ḥamāmatayni dhakaran wa-unthā
sentences.l: And she saw among the birds two doves, a male and a female.
sentences.i: Among the birds she saw two doves, a male and a female.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هِيَ تَنْظُرُ إِلَى الشَّرَكِ وَإِذَا بِرِجْلِ الذَّكَرِ تَعَلَّقَتْ فِى الشَّرَكِ وَصَارَ يَخْتَبِطُ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hiya tanẓuru ilā al-sharaki wa-idhā bi-rijli al-dhakari taʿallaqat fī al-sharaki wa-ṣāra yakhtabiṭu
sentences.l: And while she (was) looking at the snare, behold, the foot of the male caught in the snare, and he began flailing.
sentences.i: And as she watched the net, the male bird's foot caught in it, and he began to thrash about.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-rijli, “and behold, the foot”: after idhā of surprise, bi- only marks what appears. rijl, “foot, leg”, is feminine, hence taʿallaqat; the kasra that marks it as rijl and not rajul, “man”, is the print's, and so is the doubling mark on taʿallaqat. ṣāra yafʿalu, “he began to do”.

sentences.t: فَنَفَرَتْ عَنْهُ جَمِيعُ الطُّيُورِ وَفَرَّتْ
sentences.tr: fa-nafarat ʿanhu jamīʿu al-ṭuyūri wa-farrat
sentences.l: And all the birds shied away from him and fled.
sentences.i: All the other birds started away from him and fled.
sentences.n: The doubling mark on farrat, “they fled”, is the print's.

sentences.t: فَرَجَعَتْ إِلَيْهِ امْرَأَتُهُ وَحَامَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَنَزَلَتْ ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمَتْ إِلَى الشَّرَكِ وَالصَّيَّادُ غَافِلٌ
sentences.tr: fa-rajaʿat ilayhi imraʾatuhu wa-ḥāmat ʿalayhi wa-nazalat thumma taqaddamat ilā al-sharaki wa-al-ṣayyādu ghāfilun
sentences.l: And his wife came-back to him, and circled over him, and came-down; then she advanced to the snare, and the fowler (was) heedless.
sentences.i: But his mate came back to him, circled over him and came down, and then went up to the net while the fowler was not looking.
sentences.n: imraʾatuhu, “his wife”: the dream tells the doves' story as a human marriage.

sentences.t: فَصَارَتْ تَنْقُرُ الْعَيْنَ الَّتِي فِيهَا رِجْلُ الذَّكَرِ وَصَارَتْ تَجْذِبُهُ بِمِنْقَارِهِ حَتَّى خَلَّصَتْ رِجْلَهُ مِنَ الشَّرَكِ وَطَارَتْ هِيَ وَإِيَّاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣārat tanquru al-ʿayna allatī fīhā rijlu al-dhakari wa-ṣārat tajdhibuhu bi-minqārihi ḥattā khallaṣat rijlahu mina al-sharaki wa-ṭārat hiya wa-iyyāhu
sentences.l: And she began pecking the mesh which in it (was) the foot of the male, and began pulling it with his beak, until she freed his foot from the snare, and she flew away, she and him.
sentences.i: She began pecking at the mesh that held the male's foot and tugging at it with her beak until she had freed his foot from the net, and away they flew, she and he together.
sentences.n: al-ʿayn, “the eye”, here the mesh or loop of the net. bi-minqārihi, “with his beak”: the print gives the female bird a masculine pronoun here, kept; the sense is her beak. tajdhibuhu, “pulling it”, is masculine too, for the mesh or the trapped bird. The kasras on rijl are the print's. ṭārat hiya wa-iyyāhu, “she flew, she and him”: Middle Arabic for “the two of them flew off”.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ الصَّيَّادُ وَأَصْلَحَ الشَّرَكَ وَقَعَدَ بَعِيدًا عَنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾa baʿda dhālika al-ṣayyādu wa-aṣlaḥa al-sharaka wa-qaʿada baʿīdan ʿanhu
sentences.l: And after that the fowler came and mended the snare and sat far from it.
sentences.i: After that the fowler came, mended the net and sat down at a distance from it.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَمْضِ غَيْرُ سَاعَةٍ حَتَّى نَزَلَتِ الطُّيُورُ وَعَلِقَ الشَّرَكُ فِى الْأُنْثَى
sentences.tr: fa-lam yamḍi ghayru sāʿatin ḥattā nazalati al-ṭuyūru wa-ʿaliqa al-sharaku fī al-unthā
sentences.l: And there did not pass other-than an hour until the birds came-down, and the snare caught on the female.
sentences.i: Hardly an hour had passed before the birds came down, and the net caught the female.
sentences.n: ʿaliqa al-sharaku fī al-unthā, “the snare caught on the female”: the net, not the bird, is the subject. sāʿa, “an hour”, here just “a short while”.

sentences.t: فَنَفَرَتْ عَنْهَا جَمِيعُ الطُّيُورِ وَمِنْ جُمْلَتِهَا الطَّيْرُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَمْ يَعُدْ لِأُنْثَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-nafarat ʿanhā jamīʿu al-ṭuyūri wa-min jumlatihā al-ṭayru al-dhakaru wa-lam yaʿud li-unthāhu
sentences.l: And all the birds shied away from her, and among their whole (was) the bird the male, and he did not return to his female.
sentences.i: All the birds started away from her, the male bird among them, and he did not come back for his mate.
sentences.n: min jumlatihā, “among their number”. lam yaʿud li-, “he did not return to (or for)”.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَ الصَّيَّادُ وَأَخَذَ الطَّيْرَةَ الْأُنْثَى وَذَبَحَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾa al-ṣayyādu wa-akhadha al-ṭayrata al-unthā wa-dhabaḥahā
sentences.l: And the fowler came and took the bird-(fem.), the female, and slaughtered her.
sentences.i: Then the fowler came, took the female bird and cut her throat.
sentences.n: al-ṭayra, a feminine “bird” made from ṭayr: colloquial, not Classical.

sentences.t: فَانْتَبَهَتْ مَرْعُوبَةً مِنْ مَنَامِهَا وَقَالَتْ كُلُّ ذَكَرٍ مِثْلُ هَذَا مَا فِيهِ خَيْرٌ وَالرِّجَالُ جَمِيعُهُمْ مَا عِنْدَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لِلنِّسَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-intabahat marʿūbatan min manāmihā wa-qālat kullu dhakarin mithlu hādhā mā fīhi khayrun wa-al-rijālu jamīʿuhum mā ʿindahum khayrun li-al-nisāʾi
sentences.l: And she woke terrified from her dream and said: Every male like this, there is not in him good; and the men, all of them, there is not with them good for the women.
sentences.i: She woke from her dream in terror and said, ‘Every male is like this one, there is no good in him; and men, all of them, have nothing good in them for women.’”
sentences.n: mā fīhi khayr, “there is no good in him”: mā as the plain negative of colloquial speech.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ حَدِيثِهَا قَالَ لَهَا تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ يَا أُمِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَنْظُرَ إِلَيْهَا نَظْرَةً وَاحِدَةً وَلَوْ كَانَ فِي ذَلِكَ مَمَاتِي فَتَحَيَّلِي لِي بِحِيلَةٍ حَتَّى أَنْظُرَ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min ḥadīthihā qāla lahā tāju al-mulūki yā ummī urīdu an anẓura ilayhā naẓratan wāḥidatan wa-law kāna fī dhālika mamātī fa-taḥayyalī lī bi-ḥīlatin ḥattā anẓura ilayhā
sentences.l: And when she finished from her talk, Tāj al-Mulūk said to her: O my mother, I want that I look at her one look, even if there were in that my death; so contrive for me a contrivance so that I look at her.
sentences.i: When she had finished her story, Tāj al-Mulūk said to her, “Mother, I want to look on her just once, even if it is the death of me; so find me some trick by which I may see her.”
sentences.n: taḥayyalī lī bi-ḥīlatin, “contrive me a contrivance”: the verb and its object come from the same root; bi- marks the means. The doubling mark on taḥayyalī is the print's.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ اعْلَمْ أَنَّ لَهَا بُسْتَانًا تَحْتَ قَصْرِهَا وَهُوَ بِرَسْمِ فُرْجَتِهَا وَأَنَّهَا تَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ مَرَّةً مِنْ بَابِ السِّرِّ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati iʿlam anna lahā bustānan taḥta qaṣrihā wa-huwa bi-rasmi furjatihā wa-annahā takhruju ilayhi fī kulli shahrin marratan min bābi al-sirri
sentences.l: And she said: Know that for her (is) a garden below her palace, and it (is) by-the-designation of her recreation; and that she goes-out to it in every month once, by the door of the secret.
sentences.i: She said, “Know that she has a garden below her palace, kept for her pleasure, and that she goes out into it once every month by the private door.
sentences.n: bi-rasmi, “appointed for, reserved for”: a Middle Arabic chancery phrase. furja, “recreation, an outing to enjoy”. bāb al-sirr, “the door of the secret”, a private or postern gate; the doubling mark on al-sirr is the print's.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ قَدْ جَاءَ أَوَانُ خُرُوجِهَا إِلَى الْفُرْجَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda ʿasharati ayyāmin qad jāʾa awānu khurūjihā ilā al-furjati
sentences.l: And after ten days has come the time of her going-out to the recreation.
sentences.i: In ten days' time comes the moment for her to go out and take her pleasure.
sentences.n: qad jāʾa, a perfect, “has come”, used of what is as good as settled.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا أَرَادَتِ الْخُرُوجَ أَجِيءُ إِلَيْكَ وَأُعْلِمُكَ حَتَّى تَخْرُجَ وَتُصَادِفَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā arādati al-khurūja ajīʾu ilayka wa-uʿlimuka ḥattā takhruja wa-tuṣādifahā
sentences.l: And when she wants the going-out, I come to you and let you know, so that you go out and come-upon her.
sentences.i: When she means to go out, I will come and let you know, so that you can go out and come across her.
sentences.n: ṣādafa, “to meet by chance, to come upon”: the meeting must look like an accident.

sentences.t: وَاحْرِصْ عَلَى أَنَّكَ لَا تُفَارِقُ الْبُسْتَانَ فَلَعَلَّهَا إِذَا رَأَتْ حُسْنَكَ وَجَمَالَكَ يَتَعَلَّقُ قَلْبُهَا بِمَحَبَّتِكَ فَإِنَّ الْمَحَبَّةَ أَعْظَمُ أَسْبَابِ الِاجْتِمَاعِ
sentences.tr: wa-iḥriṣ ʿalā annaka lā tufāriqu al-bustāna fa-laʿallahā idhā raʾat ḥusnaka wa-jamālaka yataʿallaqu qalbuhā bi-maḥabbatika fa-inna al-maḥabbata aʿẓamu asbābi al-ijtimāʿi
sentences.l: And be-careful about that you do not leave the garden; for perhaps she, when she sees your beauty and your comeliness, her heart attaches to love of you; for the love (is) the greatest of the causes of the coming-together.
sentences.i: And take care that you do not leave the garden; for it may be that when she sees your beauty and grace her heart will be caught by love of you, and love is the strongest of all the bonds that bring people together.”
sentences.n: ḥariṣa ʿalā, “to be intent on, to take care to”. taʿallaqa qalbuhu bi-, “his heart became attached to”: the verb takes bi-.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And he said: (With) hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: He said, “With hearing and obedience.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَ مِنَ الدُّكَّانِ هُوَ وَعَزِيزٌ وَأَخَذَا مَعَهُمَا الْعَجُوزَ وَمَضَيَا إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِمَا وَعَرَّفَاهُ لَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma qāma mina al-dukkāni huwa wa-ʿazīzun wa-akhadhā maʿahumā al-ʿajūza wa-maḍayā ilā manzilihimā wa-ʿarrafāhu lahā
sentences.l: Then he rose from the shop, he and ʿAzīz, and they-two took with them the old woman and went to their dwelling and made it known to her.
sentences.i: Then he and ʿAzīz left the shop, took the old woman with them and went to their lodging, and showed her where it was.
sentences.n: qāma … huwa wa-ʿazīz, “he rose, he and ʿAzīz”: the verb is singular, the following verbs dual. ʿarrafāhu lahā, “they made it known to her”: Classical would say ʿarrafāhā iyyāhu; li- marks the one told, as with nāwala li- above.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ قَالَ لِعَزِيزٍ يَا أَخِي لَيْسَ لِي حَاجَةٌ بِالدُّكَّانِ وَقَدْ قَضَيْتُ حَاجَتِي مِنْهَا وَوَهَبْتُهَا لَكَ بِجَمِيعِ مَا فِيهَا لِأَنَّكَ تَغَرَّبْتَ مَعِي وَفَارَقْتَ بِلَادَكَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna tāja al-mulūki qāla li-ʿazīzin yā akhī laysa lī ḥājatun bi-al-dukkāni wa-qad qaḍaytu ḥājatī minhā wa-wahabtuhā laka bi-jamīʿi mā fīhā li-annaka tagharrabta maʿī wa-fāraqta bilādaka
sentences.l: Then Tāj al-Mulūk said to ʿAzīz: O my brother, there is not for me need of the shop, and I have accomplished my need from it; and I have given it to you with all that (is) in it, because you went-abroad with me and left your country.
sentences.i: Then Tāj al-Mulūk said to ʿAzīz, “Brother, I have no more need of the shop; it has done what I needed of it. I give it to you, with everything in it, because you have gone into exile with me and left your own country.”
sentences.n: The print has وفارتت, a misprint for وفارقت, wa-fāraqta, “and you left”, corrected here. ḥāja bi-, “need of”. The shop, dukkān, is treated as feminine here (minhā, wahabtuhā, fīhā). bi-jamīʿi mā fīhā, “with all that is in it”: bi- of accompaniment. The doubling mark on tagharrabta, “you became a stranger, went abroad”, is the print's.

sentences.t: فَقَبِلَ عَزِيزٌ مِنْهُ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ جَلَسَا يَتَحَدَّثَانِ وَصَارَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ يَسْئَلُهُ عَنْ غَرِيبِ أَحْوَالِهِ وَمَا جَرَى لَهُ وَصَارَ هُوَ يُخْبِرُهُ بِمَا حَصَلَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qabila ʿazīzun minhu dhālika thumma jalasā yataḥaddathāni wa-ṣāra tāju al-mulūki yasʾaluhu ʿan gharībi aḥwālihi wa-mā jarā lahu wa-ṣāra huwa yukhbiruhu bi-mā ḥaṣala lahu
sentences.l: And ʿAzīz accepted that from him; then they-two sat talking, and Tāj al-Mulūk began asking him about the strange of his circumstances and what happened to him, and he began informing him of what befell him.
sentences.i: ʿAzīz accepted it from him, and then the two of them sat and talked; Tāj al-Mulūk asked him about his strange adventures and all that had happened to him, and ʿAzīz told him everything that had befallen him.
sentences.n: The print spells yasʾaluhu with its hamza on a yāʾ seat (يسئله), an older spelling. akhbara bi-, “to tell of”: the verb takes bi-.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَقْبَلَا عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ وَأَعْلَمَاهُ بِمَا عَزَمَ عَلَيْهِ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَقَالَا لَهُ كَيْفَ الْعَمَلُ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika aqbalā ʿalā al-wazīri wa-aʿlamāhu bi-mā ʿazama ʿalayhi tāju al-mulūki wa-qālā lahu kayfa al-ʿamalu
sentences.l: And after that the two came-forward to the vizier and informed him of what Tāj al-Mulūk had resolved upon, and the two said to him: How (is) the doing?
sentences.i: After that the two of them went to the vizier, told him what Tāj al-Mulūk had resolved on, and said to him, “What is to be done?”
sentences.n: aqbalā, aʿlamāhu, qālā: dual verbs, for Tāj al-Mulūk and ʿAzīz together. aʿlamahu bi-, “to inform someone of”: the verb takes bi-. kayfa al-ʿamal, “how is the doing?”, means “what do we do now?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ قُومُوا بِنَا إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla qūmū binā ilā al-bustāni
sentences.l: And he said: Rise (and go) with us to the garden.
sentences.i: He said, “Come, let us go to the garden.”
sentences.n: qūmū binā, “rise with us”: bi- of accompaniment, the everyday “come, let's go”.

sentences.t: فَلَبِسَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ أَفْخَرَ مَا عِنْدَهُ وَخَرَجُوا وَخَلْفَهُمْ ثَلٰثَةُ مَمَالِيكَ وَتَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-labisa kullu wāḥidin minhum afkhara mā ʿindahu wa-kharajū wa-khalfahum thalāthatu mamālīka wa-tawajjahū ilā al-bustāni
sentences.l: And each one of them put on the most-splendid of what (was) with him, and they went out, and behind them three mamlūks, and they headed to the garden.
sentences.i: Each of them put on the finest clothes he had, and they went out with three mamlūks behind them and made for the garden.
sentences.n: The print spells thalātha, “three”, without its long alif (ثلثة); the small alif over the lām is ours. mamālīk, “mamlūks”, slave attendants. The print marks the doubled jīm of tawajjahū with its own shadda.

sentences.t: فَرَأَوْهُ كَثِيرَ الْأَشْجَارِ غَزِيرَ الْأَنْهَارِ وَرَأَوُا الْخَوْلِيَّ جَالِسًا عَلَى الْبَابِ فَسَلَّمُوا عَلَيْهِ فَرَدَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾawhu kathīra al-ashjāri ghazīra al-anhāri wa-raʾawu al-khawliyya jālisan ʿalā al-bābi fa-sallamū ʿalayhi fa-radda ʿalayhimu al-salāma
sentences.l: And they saw it many of the trees, abundant of the streams; and they saw the gardener sitting at the gate, and they greeted him, and he returned to them the greeting.
sentences.i: They found it thick with trees and full of running streams, and saw the gardener sitting at the gate. They greeted him, and he returned their greeting.
sentences.n: kathīr al-ashjār, ghazīr al-anhār, “many of trees, abundant of streams”: a rhymed pair. al-khawlī, “the gardener, the keeper of an orchard”, an Egyptian word; a few lines on the same man is al-bustānī and al-shaykh. The print marks sallamū and radda with their own doubling marks.

sentences.t: فَنَاوَلَهُ الْوَزِيرُ مِائَةَ دِينَارٍ وَقَالَ أَشْتَهِي أَنْ تَأْخُذَ هَذِهِ النَّفَقَةَ وَتَشْتَرِيَ لَنَا شَيْأً نَأْكُلُهُ فَإِنَّنَا غُرَبَاءُ وَمَعِي هَؤُلَاءِ الْأَوْلَادُ وَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُفَرِّجَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-nāwalahu al-wazīru miʾata dīnārin wa-qāla ashtahī an taʾkhudha hādhihi al-nafaqata wa-tashtariya lanā shayʾan naʾkuluhu fa-innanā ghurabāʾu wa-maʿī hāʾulāʾi al-awlādu wa-aradtu an ufarrijahum
sentences.l: And the vizier handed him a hundred dinars and said: I desire that you take this the spending-money and buy for us a thing (that) we eat it, for we (are) strangers, and with me (are) these the boys, and I wanted that I give-them-an-outing.
sentences.i: The vizier handed him a hundred dinars and said, “I would like you to take this for expenses and buy us something to eat, for we are strangers here; I have these young men with me and wanted to show them the sights.”
sentences.n: nafaqa, “expenses, money for spending”. The print spells shayʾan as شيأ, and taʾkhudh, naʾkul without their hamza. farraja, “to give someone a pleasant outing”, is from the same root as furja, “sightseeing”.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الْبُسْتَانِيُّ الدَّنَانِيرَ وَقَالَ لَهُمُ ادْخُلُوا وَتَفَرَّجُوا وَجَمِيعُهُ مِلْكُكُمْ وَاجْلِسُوا حَتَّى أُحْضِرَ لَكُمْ بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-bustāniyyu al-danānīra wa-qāla lahumu udkhulū wa-tafarrajū wa-jamīʿuhu milkukum wa-ijlisū ḥattā uḥḍira lakum bi-mā taʾkulūna
sentences.l: And the gardener took the dinars and said to them: Enter and take-your-pleasure, and all of it (is) your property; and sit, until I bring for you (with) what you will eat.
sentences.i: The gardener took the dinars and said to them, “Come in and enjoy yourselves; it is all yours. Sit down, and I will bring you something to eat.”
sentences.n: tafarrajū, “enjoy the sights”, again the root of furja. jamīʿuhu milkukum, “all of it is your property”, is a courteous formula, not a gift. aḥḍara bi-, “to bring”: in Classical Arabic aḥḍara takes a direct object; here it borrows the bi- of atā bi-, “to come with”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى السُّوقِ وَدَخَلَ الْوَزِيرُ وَتَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَعَزِيزٌ دَاخِلَ الْبُسْتَانِ بَعْدَ أَنْ ذَهَبَ الْبُسْتَانِيُّ إِلَى السُّوقِ
sentences.tr: thumma tawajjaha ilā al-sūqi wa-dakhala al-wazīru wa-tāju al-mulūki wa-ʿazīzun dākhila al-bustāni baʿda an dhahaba al-bustāniyyu ilā al-sūqi
sentences.l: Then he headed to the market; and the vizier and Tāj al-Mulūk and ʿAzīz went in, inside the garden, after the gardener had gone to the market.
sentences.i: Then he set off for the market, and once he had gone, the vizier, Tāj al-Mulūk and ʿAzīz went into the garden.
sentences.n: dakhala … dākhila al-bustān, “went in … inside the garden”: the doubling is the narrator's own.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ أَتَى وَمَعَهُ خَارُوفٌ مَشْوِيٌّ وَخُبْزٌ مِثْلُ الْقُطْنِ وَوَضَعَهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ فَأَكَلُوا وَشَرِبُوا
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda sāʿatin atā wa-maʿahu khārūfun mashwiyyun wa-khubzun mithlu al-quṭni wa-waḍaʿahu bayna aydīhim fa-akalū wa-sharibū
sentences.l: Then after an hour he came, and with him a sheep roasted and bread like the cotton, and he set it between their hands; and they ate and drank.
sentences.i: After a while he came back with a roast lamb and bread as soft and white as cotton, and set it before them, and they ate and drank.
sentences.n: khārūf, “a sheep, a lamb”, with a long ā, is the spoken form of Classical kharūf; kept. sāʿa, “an hour”, often just “a while”. bayna aydīhim, “between their hands”, is “before them”.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَحْضَرَ لَهُمْ حَلْوَى فَتَحَلَّوْا وَغَسَلُوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَجَلَسُوا يُحَدِّثُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika aḥḍara lahum ḥalwā fa-taḥallaw wa-ghasalū aydiyahum wa-jalasū yuḥaddithūna
sentences.l: And after that he brought to them sweetmeat, and they took-sweets, and washed their hands, and sat talking.
sentences.i: After that he brought them sweets, and they ate them, washed their hands and sat talking.
sentences.n: taḥallā, “to eat sweets”, is made from the same root as ḥalwā, “sweetmeat”. yuḥaddithūna, “talking”: Classical would have yataḥaddathūna, “talking together”, which the text itself uses a page later.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ أَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ هَذَا الْبُسْتَانِ هَلْ هُوَلَكَ أَمْ أَنْتَ مُسْتَأْجِرُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru akhbirnī ʿan hādhā al-bustāni hal huwa laka am anta mustaʾjiruhu
sentences.l: And the vizier said: Tell me about this garden: is it yours, or (are) you its renter?
sentences.i: The vizier said, “Tell me about this garden. Is it yours, or do you rent it?”
sentences.n: The print runs huwa laka, “it (is) yours”, together as one word (هولك), and does the same in the answer (ماهولي). mustaʾjir, “one who hires or rents”; the print leaves out the hamza (مستاجره).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ مَاهُوَلِي وَإِنَّمَا هُوَ لِبِنْتِ الْمَلِكِ السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu mā huwa lī wa-innamā huwa li-binti al-maliki al-sayyidati dunyā
sentences.l: And the old-man said: Not it (is) mine; it is only for the daughter of the king, the Lady Dunyā.
sentences.i: The old man said, “It is not mine; it belongs to the king's daughter, the Lady Dunyā.”
sentences.n: mā huwa lī, “it is not mine”, run together in the print (ماهولي). li-, “belonging to”, marks the owner. al-shaykh, “the old man”, is the gardener.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ كَمْ لَكَ فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ مِنَ الْأُجْرَةِ فَقَالَ دِينَارٌ وَاحِدٌ لَا غَيْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru kam laka fī kulli shahrin mina al-ujrati fa-qāla dīnārun wāḥidun lā ghayru
sentences.l: And the vizier said: How much (is) for you in every month of the wage? And he said: One dinar, not other.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “How much do you get each month in wages?” He said, “One dinar, no more.”
sentences.n: lā ghayru, “not other”, is “and nothing more”.

sentences.t: فَتَأَمَّلَ الْوَزِيرُ فِى الْبُسْتَانِ فَرَأَى هُنَاكَ قَصْرًا عَالِيًا إِلَّا أَنَّهُ عَتِيقٌ
sentences.tr: fa-taʾammala al-wazīru fī al-bustāni fa-raʾā hunāka qaṣran ʿāliyan illā annahu ʿatīqun
sentences.l: And the vizier looked-closely in the garden, and saw there a palace lofty — except that it (was) old.
sentences.i: The vizier looked about the garden and saw there a lofty palace, but an old one.
sentences.n: qaṣr, “palace”, here a garden pavilion. The print marks the doubled lām of illā with its own shadda (الّا), and spells fī, “in”, with a final ى.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ يَا شَيْخُ أُرِيدُأَنْ أَعْمَلَ هُنَا خَيْرًا تَذْكُرُنِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru yā shaykhu urīdu an aʿmala hunā khayran tadhkurunī bihi
sentences.l: And the vizier said: O old-man, I want that I do here a good (work) (that) you will remember me by it.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “Old man, I should like to do some good work here that you will remember me by.”
sentences.n: The print runs urīdu an, “I want that”, into one word (اريدان), and in the next sentence turīdu an (تريدان); the spacing is kept. khayr, “good”, here a good deed, a benefaction. dhakarahu bi-, “to remember someone by”: bi- marks the thing that recalls him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي وَمَا تُرِيدُأَنْ تَفْعَلَ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidī wa-mā turīdu an tafʿala mina al-khayri
sentences.l: And he said: O my master, and what do you want that you do of the good?
sentences.i: He said, “My lord, and what good would you like to do?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ خُذْ هَذِةِ الثَّلٰثَمِائَةِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla khudh hādhihi al-thalāthamiʾati dīnārin
sentences.l: And he said: Take these the three-hundred dinar.
sentences.i: He said, “Take these three hundred dinars.”
sentences.n: The print has الثلٰمائة, a misprint for al-thalāthamiʾa (الثلٰثمائة), “the three hundred”, corrected here; the small alif over the lām is the print's own. After a hundred the counted noun stands in the singular: “three hundred dinar”. The print spells hādhihi with ة (هذة).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَوْلِيُّ بِذِكْرِ الذَّهَبِ قَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي مَهْمَا شِئْتَ فَافْعَلْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khawliyyu bi-dhikri al-dhahabi qāla yā sayyidī mahmā shiʾta fa-ifʿal
sentences.l: And when the gardener heard of the mention of the gold, he said: O my master, whatever you wished, then do (it).
sentences.i: When the gardener heard gold mentioned, he said, “My lord, do whatever you like.”
sentences.n: samiʿa bi-, “to hear of”: bi- marks the news that reaches the ear.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَعْطَاهُ الدَّنَانِيرَ وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنْشَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى نَفْعَلُ فِي هَذَا الْمَحَلِّ خَيْرًا
sentences.tr: thumma aʿṭāhu al-danānīra wa-qāla lahu in shāʾa allāhu taʿālā nafʿalu fī hādhā al-maḥalli khayran
sentences.l: Then he gave him the dinars and said to him: If God, exalted (is He), wills, we will do in this the place a good (work).
sentences.i: Then he gave him the dinars and said, “God willing, we shall do some good work in this place.”
sentences.n: The print sets in shāʾa allāh, “if God wills”, as one word, انشاء, which looks like inshāʾ, “composition”; it is read as the familiar formula and the spelling is kept. taʿālā, “exalted is He”, follows the name of God.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجُوا مِنْ عِنْدِهِ وَتَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِمْ وَبَاتُوا تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ
sentences.tr: thumma kharajū min ʿindihi wa-tawajjahū ilā manzilihim wa-bātū tilka al-laylata
sentences.l: Then they went out from his presence, and headed to their lodging, and spent-the-night that night.
sentences.i: Then they took their leave of him, went back to their lodging and spent the night there.
sentences.n: min ʿindihi, “from with him”, is “from his presence”. bāta, “to spend the night”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ مِنَ الْغَدِ أَحْضَرَ الْوَزِيرُ مُبَيِّضًا وَنَقَّاشًا وَصَائِغًا جَيِّدًا وَأَحْضَرَ لَهُمْ جَمِيعَ مَايَحْتَاجُونَ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْآلَاتِ وَدَخَلَ بِهِمُ الْبُسْتَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna mina al-ghadi aḥḍara al-wazīru mubayyiḍan wa-naqqāshan wa-ṣāʾighan jayyidan wa-aḥḍara lahum jamīʿa mā yaḥtājūna ilayhi mina al-ālāti wa-dakhala bihimu al-bustāna
sentences.l: And when it was of the morrow, the vizier brought a whitewasher and a painter and a goldsmith, a good (one), and brought for them all (that) they need of the tools, and entered with them the garden.
sentences.i: Next day the vizier brought a plasterer, a painter and a skilled goldsmith, fetched them all the tools they needed and took them into the garden.
sentences.n: mubayyiḍ, “whitener”, one who whitewashes or plasters walls; naqqāsh, “engraver, decorator”, here a painter of walls; ṣāʾigh, “goldsmith”, wanted for the gilding. The print marks the doubled letters of mubayyiḍ, naqqāsh and jayyid. mā yaḥtājūna, “what they need”, is run together (مايحتاجون). dakhala bi-, “to enter with”, is to bring someone in.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَهُمْ بِتَبْيِيضِ ذَلِكَ الْقَصْرِ وَزَخْرَفَتِهِ بِأَنْوَاعِ النَّقْشِ
sentences.tr: wa-amarahum bi-tabyīḍi dhālika al-qaṣri wa-zakhrafatihi bi-anwāʿi al-naqshi
sentences.l: And he ordered them (to) the whitening of that palace and its adorning with the kinds of the decoration.
sentences.i: He ordered them to whitewash the palace and adorn it with every kind of painted ornament.
sentences.n: amara bi-, “to order (something)”: the verb takes bi- for the thing commanded. bi-anwāʿ, “with kinds”: bi- of means.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِ الذَّهَبِ وَاللَّازَوَرْدِ وَقَالَ لِلنَّقَّاشِ اعْمَلْ فِي صَدْرِ هَذَا الْإِيوَانِ صُورَةَ آدَمِيٍّ صَيَّادٍ كَأَنَّهُ نَصَبَ شَرَكَهُ وَقَدْ وَقَعَتْ فِيهِ طُيُورٌ وَحَمَامَةٌ وَاشْتَبَكَتْ بِمِنْقَارِهَا فِى الشَّرَكِ
sentences.tr: thumma amara bi-iḥḍāri al-dhahabi wa-al-lāzawardi wa-qāla li-al-naqqāshi iʿmal fī ṣadri hādhā al-īwāni ṣūrata ādamiyyin ṣayyādin kaʾannahu naṣaba sharakahu wa-qad waqaʿat fīhi ṭuyūrun wa-ḥamāmatun wa-ishtabakat bi-minqārihā fī al-sharaki
sentences.l: Then he ordered the bringing of the gold and the lapis-lazuli, and said to the painter: Make in the breast of this the hall a picture of a human, a hunter, as-though he had set his net, and there had fallen into it birds, and a dove, and it was entangled by its beak in the net.
sentences.i: Then he had gold and lapis lazuli brought, and said to the painter, “At the head of this hall paint the figure of a man, a fowler, who seems to have set his net; birds have fallen into it, and a dove has caught its beak in the mesh.”
sentences.n: amara bi-, “to order”, again takes bi-. lāzaward, “lapis lazuli”, ground for blue paint. ṣadr, “breast”, of a room: the wall facing the entrance, the place of honour. īwān, “a hall open on one side”. ādamī, “a son of Adam”, a human being. The print marks the doubled yāʾ of ṣayyād.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَقَشَ النَّقَّاشُ جَانِبًا وَفَرَغَ مِنْ نَقْشِهِ قَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ افْعَلْ فِى الْجَانِبِ الْآخَرِ مِثْلَ الْأَوَّلِ وَصَوِّرْ صُورَةَ الْحَمَامَةِ وَحْدَهَا فِى الشَّرَكِ وَأَنَّ الصَّيَّادَ أَخَذَهَا وَوَضَعَ السِّكِّينَ عَلَى رَقَبَتِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naqasha al-naqqāshu jāniban wa-faragha min naqshihi qāla lahu al-wazīru ifʿal fī al-jānibi al-ākhari mithla al-awwali wa-ṣawwir ṣūrata al-ḥamāmati waḥdahā fī al-sharaki wa-anna al-ṣayyāda akhadhahā wa-waḍaʿa al-sikkīna ʿalā raqabatihā
sentences.l: And when the painter had painted a side and finished from his painting, the vizier said to him: Do on the side the other like the first, and picture the picture of the dove alone in the net, and that the hunter has taken it and put the knife on its neck.
sentences.i: When the painter had finished one side, the vizier said to him, “Do the same on the other side, but show the dove alone in the net, and the fowler taking it and setting the knife to its throat.”
sentences.n: wa-anna al-ṣayyāda akhadhahā, “and that the hunter has taken it”, hangs loosely on ṣawwir, “paint”: paint how the hunter has taken it. The print marks the doubled wāw of ṣawwir.

sentences.t: وَاعْمَلْ فِى الْجَانِبِ الْآخَرِ صُورَةَ جَارِحٍ كَبِيرٍ قَدْ قَنَصَ ذَكَرَ الْحَمَامِ وَأَنْشَبَ فِيهِ مَخَالِبَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿmal fī al-jānibi al-ākhari ṣūrata jāriḥin kabīrin qad qanaṣa dhakara al-ḥamāmi wa-anshaba fīhi makhālibahu
