sentences.l: And make on the side the other a picture of a raptor big (that) has hunted the male of the doves and stuck in it its talons.
sentences.i: And on the other side paint a great bird of prey that has caught the male dove and driven its talons into him.
sentences.n: jāriḥ, “a hunting bird, a raptor”. “The other side” again: a third wall, or the narrator not counting carefully. dhakar al-ḥamām, “the male of the doves”, is the dove's mate. The pictures are meant for the Lady Dunyā, who hates men because of a dream in which a male bird left his mate caught in a net; here the male does not desert her, he is carried off.

sentences.t: فَفَعَلَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-faʿala dhālika
sentences.l: And he did that.
sentences.i: The painter did all this.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغُوا مِنْ هَذِةِ الْأَشْيَاءِ الَّتِى ذَكَرَهَا الْوَزِيرُ وَأَعْطَاهُمْ أُجْرَتَهُمُ انْصَرَفُوا وَانْصَرَفَ الْوَزِيرُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ وَوَدَّعُوا الْبُسْتَانِيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghū min hādhihi al-ashyāʾi allatī dhakarahā al-wazīru wa-aʿṭāhum ujratahumu inṣarafū wa-inṣarafa al-wazīru wa-man maʿahu wa-waddaʿū al-bustāniyya
sentences.l: And when they had finished from these the things which the vizier mentioned, and he had given them their wage, they went-away; and the vizier and who (was) with him went-away, and they bade-farewell-to the gardener.
sentences.i: When they had finished everything the vizier had asked for and he had paid them, they went away; and the vizier and his companions left too, taking leave of the gardener.
sentences.n: The print spells hādhihi with ة (هذة) and allatī with a final ى (التى), and marks the doubled dāl of waddaʿū.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِمْ وَجَلَسُوا يَتَحَدَّثُونَ
sentences.tr: thumma tawajjahū ilā manzilihim wa-jalasū yataḥaddathūna
sentences.l: Then they headed to their lodging and sat talking-together.
sentences.i: Then they went back to their lodging and sat talking.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ لِعَزِيزٍ يَا أَخِي أَنْشِدْنِي بَعْضَ الْأَشْعَارِ لَعَلَّ صَدْرِي يَنْشَرِحُ وَتَزُولُ عَنِّي هَذِهِ الْأَفْكَارُ وَيَبْرُدُ مَا بِقَلْبِي مِنْ لَهِيبِ النَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla tāju al-mulūki li-ʿazīzin yā akhī anshidnī baʿḍa al-ashʿāri laʿalla ṣadrī yansharihu wa-tazūlu ʿannī hādhihi al-afkāru wa-yabrudu mā bi-qalbī min lahībi al-nāri
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk said to ʿAzīz: O my brother, recite-to-me some of the poems; perhaps my breast will open-out, and there will pass from me these the thoughts, and will cool what (is) in my heart of the flame of the fire.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk said to ʿAzīz, “Brother, recite me some poetry; perhaps my heart will lighten, these cares will leave me, and the fire that burns in my heart will cool.”
sentences.n: inshiraḥ al-ṣadr, “the opening of the breast”, is relief and gladness. afkār, “thoughts”, here anxious, lovesick ones; afkār and nār rhyme. bi-qalbī, “in my heart”: bi- of place.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَطْرَبَ عَزِيزٌ بِالنَّغَمَاتِ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika aṭraba ʿazīzun bi-al-naghamāti wa-anshada hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: So at that ʿAzīz made-delight with the melodies and recited these verses:
sentences.i: Then ʿAzīz sang out tunefully and recited these verses:
sentences.n: aṭraba bi-al-naghamāt, “moved (his hearers) to delight with melodies”: he chanted the verses to a tune, bi- marking the means.

sentences.t:
جَمِيعُ مَا قَالَتِ الْعُشَّاقُ مِنْ كَمَدٍ * حَوَيْتُهُ مُفْرَدًا حَتَّى وَهَى جَلَدِى
وَاِنْ تُرِدْ مَوْرِدًا مِنْ ادمعِي اتَّسَعَتْ * لِلْوَارِدِينَ بِحَارُ الدَّمْعِ فِي مَدَدِ
وَاِنْ تُرِدْ تَنْظُرُ الْعُشَّاقَ مَا صَنَعَتْ * اَيْدِى الْغَرَامِ بِهِمْ فَانْظُرْ اِلَى جَسَدِى
sentences.tr:
jamīʿu mā qālati al-ʿushshāqu min kamadin * ḥawaytuhu mufradan ḥattā wahā jaladī
wa-in turid mawridan min admuʿī ittasaʿat * li-al-wāridīna biḥāru al-damʿi fī madadi
wa-in turid tanẓuru al-ʿushshāqa mā ṣanaʿat * aydī al-gharāmi bihim fa-nẓur ilā jasadī
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed; the print marks only the ʿayn of admuʿī, “my tears” (ادمعِي). wahā, “grew weak”, is spelled with ى. turid tanẓuru, “you want (to) see”, sets the second verb beside the first without an, “to”. madad, “supply, reinforcement”: the seas of tears never run short.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَفَاضَ الْعَبَرَاتِ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma afāḍa al-ʿabarāti wa-anshada hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then he poured-out the tears and recited these verses:
sentences.i: Then he let his tears flow and recited these verses:

sentences.t:
مَنْ كَانَ لَا يَعْشِقُ الْاَجْيَادَ وَالْحُدَقَ * ثُمَّ ادَّعَى لَذَّةَ الدُّنْيَا فَمَا صَدَقَ
فَاِنَّ فِي الْعِشْقِ مَعْنًى لَيْسَ يُدْرِكُهُ * مِنَ الْبَرِيَّةِ اِلَّا كُلُّ مَنْ عَشِقَ
لَا خَفَّفَ اللّٰهُ عَنْ قَلْبِي صَبَابَتَهُ * بِمَنْ هَوَيْتُ وَلَا عَنْ جَفْنِيَ الْاَرَقَ
sentences.tr:
man kāna lā yaʿshiqu al-ajyāda wa-al-ḥadaqa * thumma iddaʿā ladhdhata al-dunyā fa-mā ṣadaqa
fa-inna fī al-ʿishqi maʿnan laysa yudrikuhu * mina al-bariyyati illā kullu man ʿashiqa
lā khaffafa allāhu ʿan qalbī ṣabābatahu * bi-man hawaytu wa-lā ʿan jafniya al-araqa
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. ajyād, “necks”, plural of jīd, and ḥadaq, “eyes”, properly the dark of the eye: a long neck and dark eyes are the stock marks of beauty. laysa yudrikuhu, “not perceives it”: laysa with a verb is simply “not”. lā khaffafa allāhu, “may God not lighten”: lā with the past tense makes a wish. bi-man hawaytu, “for the one I love”: bi- gives what the longing is for.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَطْرَبَ بِالنَّغَمَاتِ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma aṭraba bi-al-naghamāti wa-anshada hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then he delighted with the melodies and recited these verses:
sentences.i: Then he sang to sweet melodies and recited these verses:
sentences.n: aṭraba bi-al-naghamāt, “he gave delight with melodies”: he sang to music; bi- of means.

sentences.t:
زَعَمَ ابْنُ سِينَا فِي اُصُولِ كَلَامِهِ * اَنَّ الْمُحِبَّ دَوَاؤُهُ الْاَلْحَانُ
وَوِصَالُ مِثْلِ حَبِيبِهِ مِنْ جِنْسِهِ * وَالنُّقْلُ وَالْمَشْرُوبُ وَالْبُسْتَانُ
فَصَحِبْتُ غَيْرَكَ لِلتَّدَاوِي مَرَّةً * وَاَعَانَنِي الْمَقْدُورُ وَالْاِمْكَانُ
فَعَلِمْتُ اَنَّ الْحُبَّ دَاءٌ قَاتِلٌ * فِيهِ ابْنُ سِينَا طِبُّهُ هَذَيَانُ
sentences.tr:
zaʿama ibnu sīnā fī uṣūli kalāmihi * anna al-muḥibba dawāʾuhu al-alḥānu
wa-wiṣālu mithli ḥabībihi min jinsihi * wa-al-nuqlu wa-al-mashrūbu wa-al-bustānu
fa-ṣaḥibtu ghayraka li-al-tadāwī marratan * wa-aʿānanī al-maqdūru wa-al-imkānu
fa-ʿalimtu anna al-ḥubba dāʾun qātilun * fīhi ibnu sīnā ṭibbuhu hadhayānu
sentences.l:
Ibn Sīnā claimed in the principles of his speech * that the lover, his remedy (is) the melodies,
And the union (with) the like of his beloved, of his kind, * and the dessert and the drink and the garden.
So I kept-company-with other-than-you for the curing, once, * and the decreed and the possible helped me;
And I knew that the love (is) a disease killing, * in which Ibn Sīnā, his medicine (is) raving.
sentences.i:
Ibn Sīnā held, in the principles he laid down, * that the lover's cure lies in music,
In union with one like his beloved, of the same kind, * in sweetmeats, and wine, and a garden.
So once, to cure myself, I took another in your place, * and fate and opportunity helped me;
And I learned that love is a deadly disease, * against which Ibn Sīnā's physic is mere raving.
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. Ibn Sīnā is Avicenna (d. 1037), the physician and philosopher, whose medical writings treat passionate love as a sickness to be cured. al-nuql, “sweetmeats”, the dried fruit and nuts taken with wine; al-mashrūb, “the drink”, is wine. ghayraka, “other than you”: the poet turns to the beloved, in the masculine. The last half-line is loose: “in it, Ibn Sīnā, his medicine is raving”, that is, against love his physic is nonsense.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ عَزِيزٌ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ تَعَجَّبَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ مِنْ فَصَاحَتِهِ وَحُسْنِ رِوَايَتِهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ قَدْ أَزَلْتَ عَنِّي بَعْضَ مَابِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha ʿazīzun min shiʿrihi taʿajjaba tāju al-mulūki min faṣāḥatihi wa-ḥusni riwāyatihi wa-qāla lahu qad azalta ʿannī baʿḍa mā bī
sentences.l: And when ʿAzīz finished from his poetry, Tāj al-Mulūk marvelled at his eloquence and the beauty of his delivery, and said to him: You have removed from me some of what (is) in me.
sentences.i: When ʿAzīz had finished his verses, Tāj al-Mulūk marvelled at his eloquence and his fine delivery, and said to him, “You have lifted some of my trouble from me.”
sentences.n: riwāya, “delivery, recitation”. mā bī, “what is in me”, is run together in the print (مابي).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ قَدْ وَقَعَ لِلْمُتَقَدِّمِينَ مَا يُحَيِّرُ السَّامِعِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru qad waqaʿa li-al-mutaqaddimīna mā yuḥayyiru al-sāmiʿīna
sentences.l: And the vizier said: There has befallen to the former-ones what bewilders the hearers.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “The poets of old have come out with things that leave their hearers amazed.”
sentences.n: waqaʿa li-, “to befall, come to”: here, what came to the poets of old to say. The words rhyme, mutaqaddimīn / sāmiʿīn.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ إِنْ كَانَ يَحْضُرُكَ شَيْءٌ مِنْ جِنْسِ هَذَا فَأَسْمِعْنِي مَا حَضَرَكَ مِنْ هَذَا الشِّعْرِ الرَّقِيقِ وَطَوِّلِ الْحَدِيثَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu in kāna yaḥḍuruka shayʾun min jinsi hādhā fa-asmiʿnī mā ḥaḍaraka min hādhā al-shiʿri al-raqīqi wa-ṭawwili al-ḥadītha
sentences.l: And he said to him: If there is coming-to-you something of the kind of this, then make me hear what has come to you of this poetry delicate, and lengthen the talk.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk said to him, “If anything of the kind comes to your mind, let me hear whatever of this tender poetry you can recall, and make the talk last.”
sentences.n: yaḥḍuruka, “is present to you”: comes to mind. asmiʿnī, “make me hear”. ṭawwili al-ḥadītha, “draw out the talk”: we read the print's طول as the imperative; read as ṭūl, “length”, it leaves the phrase hanging.

sentences.t: فَأَطْرَبَ بِالنَّغَمَاتِ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-aṭraba bi-al-naghamāti wa-anshada hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: So he delighted with the melodies and recited these verses:
sentences.i: So the vizier sang to sweet melodies and recited these verses:

sentences.t:
قَدْ كُنْتُ اَحْسِبُ اَنَّ وَصْلَكَ يُشْتَرَى * بِكَرَائِمِ الْاَمْوَالِ وَالْاَشْبَاحِ
وَظَنَنْتُ […] اَنَّ حُبَّكَ دَيِّنٌ * […] عَلَيْهِ نَفَائِسُ الْاَرْبَاحِ
حَتَّى رَاَيْتُكَ تَجْتَنِي وَتَخُصُّ مِنْ * […] […] الْاَمْنَاحِ
[…] اَنَّكَ لَا تُنَالُ بِحِيلَةٍ * وَلَوَيْتُ رَاسِي […] لِي جَنَاحِيْ
وَجَعَلْتَ بِي عُشِّ […] قَاسِمِي * فِيهِ غُدُوِّي دَائِمًا وَرَوَاحِي
sentences.tr:
qad kuntu aḥsibu anna waṣlaka yushtarā * bi-karāʾimi al-amwāli wa-al-ashbāḥi
wa-ẓanantu […] anna ḥubbaka dayyinun * […] ʿalayhi nafāʾisu al-arbāḥi
ḥattā raʾaytuka tajtanī wa-takhuṣṣu min * […] […] al-amnāḥi
[…] annaka lā tunālu bi-ḥīlatin * wa-lawaytu rāsī […] lī janāḥī
wa-jaʿalta bī ʿushshi […] qāsimī * fīhi ghuduwwī dāʾiman wa-rawāḥī
sentences.n: The vizier's poem is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. The type of its last four lines is broken in the copy this edition was read from: six words could not be read and are shown as […], and the translation of these lines is therefore partly conjectural. Several other words in them were read from damaged type: dayyin, “pious” or “in debt”, makes little sense and is perhaps a broken hayyin, “easy”, which our English follows; al-amnāḥ, “the gifts”, is an unusual plural (of minḥa) and may be misread; qāsimī, “my sharer”, is a guess at the sense. ashbāḥ, “forms, bodies”: lives given as a price. rāsī is raʾsī, “my head”, without its hamza. ghuduww and rawāḥ are going out at morning and coming home at evening: the whole round of the day.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ هَؤُلَاءِ وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْعَجُوزِ فَإِنَّهَا انْقَطَعَتْ فِي بَيْتِهَا
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri hāʾulāʾi wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-ʿajūzi fa-innahā inqaṭaʿat fī baytihā
sentences.l: This (is) what was of the affair of these; and as for what was of the affair of the old woman, she cut-herself-off in her house.
sentences.i: So much for them. As for the old woman, she kept to her house.
sentences.n: hādhā mā kāna min amri …, wa-ammā …, “this is what happened with …; and as for …”: the storyteller's formula for changing scenes. inqaṭaʿat, “she was cut off”: she stayed away.

sentences.t: وَاشْتَاقَتْ بِنْتُ الْمَلِكِ إِلَى الْفُرْجَةِ فِى الْبُسْتَانِ وَهِيَ لَاتَخْرُجُ إِلَّا بِالْعَجُوزِ
sentences.tr: wa-ishtāqat bintu al-maliki ilā al-furjati fī al-bustāni wa-hiya lā takhruju illā bi-al-ʿajūzi
sentences.l: And the daughter of the king longed for the sightseeing in the garden, and she does not go out except with the old woman.
sentences.i: Now the king's daughter longed for an outing in the garden, and she never went out without the old woman.
sentences.n: bi-al-ʿajūz, “with the old woman”: bi- of company. lā takhruju, “she does not go out”, is run together in the print (لاتخرج).

sentences.t: فَأَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهَا وَصَالَحَتْهَا وَطَيَّبَتْ خَاطِرَهَا وَقَالَتْ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَخْرُجَ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ لِأَتَفَرَّجَ عَلَى أَشْجَارِهِ وَأَثْمَارِهِ وَ يَنْشَرِحَ صَدْرِي بِأَزْهَارِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-arsalat ilayhā wa-ṣālaḥathā wa-ṭayyabat khāṭirahā wa-qālat innī urīdu an akhruja ilā al-bustāni li-atafarraja ʿalā ashjārihi wa-athmārihi wa-yanshariḥa ṣadrī bi-azhārihi
sentences.l: So she sent to her and made-peace-with her and sweetened her mind, and said: I want that I go out to the garden, that I may gaze-with-pleasure on its trees and its fruits, and my breast be-opened with its flowers.
sentences.i: So she sent for her, made peace with her and soothed her feelings, and said, “I want to go out to the garden, to enjoy the sight of its trees and its fruits, and let my heart be gladdened by its flowers.”
sentences.n: ṭayyabat khāṭirahā, “she sweetened her mind”: she soothed her. tafarraja ʿalā, “to look with pleasure at”. inshirāḥ al-ṣadr, “the opening of the breast”, is gladness; bi-azhārihi, “by its flowers”: bi- of cause. The rhyme ashjārihi / athmārihi / azhārihi is the text's own. The print breaks wa-, “and”, from its verb at the end of a line, and the gap is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا الْعَجُوزُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً وَلَكِنْ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ إِلَى بَيْتِي وَأَلْبَسَ أَثْوَابِي وَأَحْضُرَ عِنْدَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā al-ʿajūzu samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan wa-lākin urīdu an adhhaba ilā baytī wa-albasa athwābī wa-aḥḍura ʿindaki
sentences.l: And the old woman said to her: (With) hearing and obedience; but I want that I go to my house and put on my garments and come (to be) with you.
sentences.i: The old woman said to her, “With hearing and obedience. But first I want to go home and put on my clothes, and then I will come to you.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا اذْهَبِي إِلَى بَيْتِكِ وَلَا تَأَخَّرِي عَنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā idhhabī ilā baytiki wa-lā taʾakhkharī ʿannī
sentences.l: And she said to her: Go to your house, and do not be-late from me.
sentences.i: She said to her, “Go home, and do not keep me waiting.”
sentences.n: lā taʾakhkharī, “do not be late”, is tataʾakhkharī with one of its two ta- dropped, as Classical allows and speech prefers.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتِ الْعَجُوزُ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا وَتَوَجَّهَتْ إِلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ تَجَهَّزْ وَالْبَسْ أَفْخَرَ أَثْوَابِكَ وَاذْهَبْ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ وَادْخُلْ عَلَى الْبُسْتَانِيِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ اخْتَفِ فِى الْبُسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajati al-ʿajūzu min ʿindihā wa-tawajjahat ilā tāji al-mulūki wa-qālat lahu tajahhaz wa-ilbas afkhara athwābika wa-idhhab ilā al-bustāni wa-udkhul ʿalā al-bustāniyyi wa-sallim ʿalayhi thumma ikhtafi fī al-bustāni
sentences.l: And the old woman went out from with her and headed to Tāj al-Mulūk and said to him: Make-yourself-ready, and put on the finest of your garments, and go to the garden, and go in to the gardener and greet him; then hide in the garden.
sentences.i: The old woman left her and went to Tāj al-Mulūk, and said to him, “Get ready, put on your finest clothes and go to the garden; go in to the gardener and greet him, and then hide yourself in the garden.”
sentences.n: min ʿindihā, “from (being) with her”. dakhala ʿalā, “to go in to (someone)”. ikhtafi, “hide yourself”, the imperative of ikhtafā. The print spells fī with ى (فى).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And he said: (With) hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: He said, “With hearing and obedience.”

sentences.t: وَجَعَلَتْ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ إِشَارَةً ثُمَّ تَوَجَّهَتْ إِلَى السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿalat baynahā wa-baynahu ishāratan thumma tawajjahat ilā al-sayyidati dunyā
sentences.l: And she made between her and between him a signal; then she headed to the Lady Dunyā.
sentences.i: She agreed on a signal with him, and then went off to the Lady Dunyā.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَهَابِهَا قَامَ الْوَزِيرُ وَعَزِيزٌ وَأَلْبَسَا تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ بَدْلَةً مِنْ أَفْخَرِ مَلَابِسِ الْمُلُوكِ تُسَاوِي خَمْسَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ وَشَدَّا فِي وَسَطِهِ حِيَاصَةً مِنَ الذَّهَبِ مُرَصَّعَةً بِالْجَوَاهِرِ وَالْمَعَادِنِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhahābihā qāma al-wazīru wa-ʿazīzun wa-albasā tāja al-mulūki badlatan min afkhari malābisi al-mulūki tusāwī khamsata ālāfi dīnārin wa-shaddā fī wasaṭihi ḥiyāṣatan mina al-dhahabi muraṣṣaʿatan bi-al-jawāhiri wa-al-maʿādini
sentences.l: And after her going, the vizier and ʿAzīz rose and the two clothed Tāj al-Mulūk (in) a suit from the finest of the clothes of the kings, (which) was worth five thousand dinars, and the two bound on his middle a girdle of the gold, inlaid with the jewels and the minerals.
sentences.i: After she had gone, the vizier and ʿAzīz got up and dressed Tāj al-Mulūk in a suit of the finest royal clothes, worth five thousand dinars, and fastened round his waist a golden girdle set with jewels and precious stones.
sentences.n: albasā, shaddā: dual verbs, the two of them. badla, “a suit of clothes”, a late word. ḥiyāṣa, “a belt, a girdle”. muraṣṣaʿa bi-, “set with”: bi- marks what is set in it. al-maʿādin, literally “the minerals”: here precious stones and metals.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ فَلَمَّا وَصَلُوا إِلَى بَابِ الْبُسْتَانِ وَجَدُوا الْخَوْلِيَّ جَالِسًا هُنَاكَ
sentences.tr: thumma tawajjahū ilā al-bustāni fa-lammā waṣalū ilā bābi al-bustāni wajadū al-khawliyya jālisan hunāka
sentences.l: Then they headed to the garden; and when they arrived at the gate of the garden they found the gardener sitting there.
sentences.i: Then they made for the garden, and when they reached its gate they found the gardener sitting there.
sentences.n: al-khawlī, “the gardener”, an Egyptian word; he is the same man as al-bustānī.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ الْبُسْتَانِيُّ نَهَضَ لَهُ عَلَى الْأَقْدَامِ وَقَابَلَهُ بِالتَّعْظِيمِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ وَفَتَحَ لَهُ الْبَابَ وَقَالَ لَهُ ادْخُلْ وَتَفَرَّجْ فِى الْبُسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhu al-bustāniyyu nahaḍa lahu ʿalā al-aqdāmi wa-qābalahu bi-al-taʿẓīmi wa-al-ikrāmi wa-fataḥa lahu al-bāba wa-qāla lahu udkhul wa-tafarraj fī al-bustāni
sentences.l: And when the gardener saw him, he rose for him on the feet and met him with the magnifying and the honouring, and opened for him the gate and said to him: Enter and take-your-pleasure in the garden.
sentences.i: When the gardener saw him he sprang to his feet for him and received him with every mark of respect and honour, opened the gate for him and said, “Come in and enjoy the garden.”
sentences.n: qābalahu bi-, “he met him with”: bi- of manner. The rhyme taʿẓīm / ikrām is the text's own.

sentences.t: وَ لَمْ يَعْلَمِ الْبُسْتَانِيُّ أَنَّ بِنْتَ الْمَلِكِ تَدْخُلُ الْبُسْتَانَ فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yaʿlami al-bustāniyyu anna binta al-maliki tadkhulu al-bustāna fī hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: And the gardener did not know that the daughter of the king enters the garden on this day.
sentences.i: The gardener did not know that the king's daughter was coming into the garden that day.
sentences.n: Again the print breaks wa-, “and”, from its word at the end of a line.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ لَمْ يَلْبَثْ إِلَّا مِقْدَارَ سَاعَةٍ وَسَمِعَ ضَجَّةً فَلَمْ يَشْعُرْ إِلَّا وَالْخَدَمُ وَالْجَوَارِي خَرَجُوا مِنْ بَابِ السِّرِّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala tāju al-mulūki lam yalbath illā miqdāra sāʿatin wa-samiʿa ḍajjatan fa-lam yashʿur illā wa-al-khadamu wa-al-jawārī kharajū min bābi al-sirri
sentences.l: And when Tāj al-Mulūk entered, he did not stay except the measure of an hour, and he heard a clamour; and he did not perceive except (that) the servants and the slave-girls had come out from the gate of the secret.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk had been inside no more than an hour when he heard a commotion, and before he knew it the servants and slave-girls were coming out of the private gate.
sentences.n: lam yashʿur illā wa-, “he did not perceive except (that) …”: before he knew it. kharajū, a masculine plural for the mixed crowd. bāb al-sirr, “the gate of the secret”, a private gate.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُمُ الْخَوْلِيُّ ذَهَبَ إِلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَأَعْلَمَهُ بِمَجِيئِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhumu al-khawliyyu dhahaba ilā tāji al-mulūki wa-aʿlamahu bi-majīʾihā
sentences.l: And when the gardener saw them, he went to Tāj al-Mulūk and informed him of her coming.
sentences.i: When the gardener saw them, he went to Tāj al-Mulūk and told him she was coming.
sentences.n: aʿlamahu bi-, “he informed him of”: the verb takes bi-. majīʾihā, “her coming”: the princess's.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا مَوْلَايَ كَيْفَ يَكُونُ الْعَمَلُ وَقَدْ أَتَتِ ابْنَةُ الْمَلِكِ السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu yā mawlāya kayfa yakūnu al-ʿamalu wa-qad atati ibnatu al-maliki al-sayyidatu dunyā
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my master, how will be the doing, and the daughter of the king, the Lady Dunyā, has come?
sentences.i: He said to him, “My lord, what is to be done? The king's daughter, the Lady Dunyā, has come!”
sentences.n: The print has انت, a misprint for atat (اتت), “has come”, corrected here. The print has ابة, a misprint for ibnat (ابنة), “daughter”, corrected here. kayfa yakūnu al-ʿamal, “how will the doing be?”: what are we to do?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ عَلَيْكَ فَإِنِّي أَخْتَفِي فِي بَعْضِ مَوَاضِعِ الْبُسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lā baʾsa ʿalayka fa-innī akhtafī fī baʿḍi mawāḍiʿi al-bustāni
sentences.l: And he said: No harm upon you, for I will hide in some of the places of the garden.
sentences.i: He said, “Don't worry; I will hide somewhere in the garden.”
sentences.n: lā baʾsa ʿalayka, “no harm upon you”: do not be troubled. The print spells baʾs without its hamza (باس).

sentences.t: فَأَوْصَاهُ الْبُسْتَانِيُّ بِغَايَةِ الِاخْتِفَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-awṣāhu al-bustāniyyu bi-ghāyati al-ikhtifāʾi
sentences.l: So the gardener enjoined him with the utmost of the hiding.
sentences.i: The gardener urged him to hide himself as well as he could.
sentences.n: fa-awṣāhu, “and he enjoined him”, is read from a damaged word and is not certain. awṣā bi-, “to enjoin, urge”: bi- marks what is urged.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَرَكَهُ وَرَاحَ
sentences.tr: thumma tarakahu wa-rāḥa
sentences.l: Then he left him and went-off.
sentences.i: Then the gardener left him and went away.
sentences.n: The gardener (al-khawlī) leaves Tāj al-Mulūk to find his own hiding place in the garden.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَتْ بِنْتُ الْمَلِكِ هِيَ وَجَوَارِيهَا وَالْعَجُوزُ فِى الْبُسْتَانِ قَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ فِي نَفْسِهَا مَتَى كَانَ الْخَدَمُ مَعَنَا فَإِنَّنَا لَا نَنَلْ مَقْصُودَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhalat bintu al-maliki hiya wa-jawārīhā wa-al-ʿajūzu fī al-bustāni qālati al-ʿajūzu fī nafsihā matā kāna al-khadamu maʿanā fa-innanā lā nanal maqṣūdanā
sentences.l: And when the daughter of the king entered, she and her slave-girls and the old woman, into the garden, the old woman said in herself: Whenever the servants are with us, then we will not attain our aim.
sentences.i: When the king's daughter came into the garden with her slave-girls and the old woman, the old woman said to herself, “As long as the servants are with us, we shall never get what we are after.”
sentences.n: The print has تالت, a misprint for qālat (قالت), “she said”, corrected here. fī nafsihā, “in herself”: to herself. matā kāna … fa-, “whenever … then”: matā used as a conditional, here “as long as”. lā nanal, “we will not attain”, is the text's own form: the verb has the short, jussive shape (nanal, not the indicative nanālu) although plain lā normally takes the indicative; perhaps it is felt as the answer to the condition. al-khadam, “the servants”: the eunuchs and attendants who escort the princess.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِابْنَةِ الْمَلِكِ يَاسَيِّدَتِي إِنِّي أَقُولُ لَكِ عَلَى شَيُ فِيهِ رَاحَةٌ لِقَلْبِكِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat li-ibnati al-maliki yā sayyidatī innī aqūlu laki ʿalā shayʾu fīhi rāḥatun li-qalbiki
sentences.l: Then she said to the daughter of the king: O my lady, I (will) tell you about a thing in which (is) rest for your heart.
sentences.i: Then she said to the king's daughter, “My lady, I have something to tell you that will ease your heart.”
sentences.n: aqūlu laki ʿalā, “I tell you about”: ʿalā for “about” is colloquial. The print spells shayʾ without its hamza (شي) and sets a ḍamma on it, though after ʿalā the case should be genitive (shayʾin); the printed mark is kept. The print runs yā sayyidatī together (ياسيدتي). li-qalbiki, “for your heart”: li- of benefit.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا قُولِي مَا عِنْدَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-sayyidatu dunyā qūlī mā ʿindaki
sentences.l: And the Lady Dunyā said: Say what (is) with you.
sentences.i: The Lady Dunyā said, “Tell me what you have to say.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ يَاسَيِّدَتِى إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ الْخَدَمَ لَاحَاجَةَ لَكِ بِهِمْ فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ وَلَا يَنْشَرِحُ صَدْرُكِ مَادَامُوا مَعَنَا فَاصْرِفِيهِمْ عَنَّا
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu yā sayyidatī inna hāʾulāʾi al-khadama lā ḥājata laki bihim fī hādhā al-waqti wa-lā yansharihu ṣadruki mā dāmū maʿanā fa-iṣrifīhim ʿannā
sentences.l: And the old woman said: O my lady, indeed these servants — no need (is) for you of them at this time, and your breast will not be-expanded as long as they (are) with us; so send them away from us.
sentences.i: The old woman said, “My lady, you have no need of these servants just now, and you will never be at your ease while they are with us; so send them away.”
sentences.n: lā ḥājata laki bihim, “there is no need for you of them”: ḥāja bi-, “need of”. The expanding of the breast (inshirāḥ al-ṣadr) is ease and good cheer. mā dāmū, “as long as they remain”. The print runs lā ḥāja and mā dāmū together (لاحاجة, ماداموا).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا صَدَقْتِ ثُمَّ صَرَفَتْهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-sayyidatu dunyā ṣadaqti thumma ṣarafathum
sentences.l: And the Lady Dunyā said: You have spoken-truly. Then she sent them away.
sentences.i: “You are right,” said the Lady Dunyā, and she sent them away.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ قَلِيلٍ تَمَشَّتْ فَصَارَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا وَإِلَى حُسْنِهَا وَجَمَالِهَا وَهِيَ لَا تَشْعُرُ بِذَلِكَ وَكُلَّمَا نَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا يُغْشَى عَلَيْهِ مِمَّا رَأَى مِنْ بَارِعِ حُسْنِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda qalīlin tamashshat fa-ṣāra tāju al-mulūki yanẓuru ilayhā wa-ilā ḥusnihā wa-jamālihā wa-hiya lā tashʿuru bi-dhālika wa-kullamā naẓara ilayhā yughshā ʿalayhi mimmā raʾā min bāriʿi ḥusnihā
sentences.l: And after a little she strolled, and Tāj al-Mulūk began looking at her and at her beauty and her comeliness, and she not perceiving that; and whenever he looked at her, he fainted from what he saw of the surpassing of her beauty.
sentences.i: After a while she went strolling, and Tāj al-Mulūk watched her, and her beauty and grace, without her knowing it; and every time he looked at her he swooned at the sight of her surpassing loveliness.
sentences.n: yughshā ʿalayhi, “it is covered over him”: he faints; the verb is an impersonal passive. After kullamā, “whenever”, the text has the imperfect yughshā where Classical prose would use the perfect: Middle Arabic. shaʿara bi-, “to be aware of”: the verb takes bi-.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتِ الْعَجُوزُ تُسَارِقُهَا فِى الْحَدِيثِ إِلَى أَنْ أَوْصَلَتْهَا إِلَى الْقَصْرِ الَّذِي أَمَرَ الْوَزِيرُ بِنَقْشِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārati al-ʿajūzu tusāriquhā fī al-ḥadīthi ilā an awṣalathā ilā al-qaṣri alladhī amara al-wazīru bi-naqshihi
sentences.l: And the old woman began stealing-her-along in the talk until she brought her to the pavilion which the vizier had ordered the painting of.
sentences.i: And the old woman drew her along with talk, so that she hardly noticed where she went, until she had brought her to the pavilion the vizier had ordered painted.
sentences.n: tusāriquhā fī al-ḥadīth, “she stole her along in talk”: kept her talking so that she went where she was led without noticing. al-qaṣr, “the palace”, is here the old pavilion in the garden that the vizier paid to have whitewashed and painted. amara bi-, “to order”: the verb takes bi- before the thing ordered.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَتْ ذَلِكَ الْقَصْرَ وَتَفَرَّجَتْ عَلَى نَقْشِهِ وَأَبْصَرَتِ الطُّيُورَ وَالصَّيَّادَ وَالْحَمَامَ فَقَالَتْ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ هَذِةِ صِفَّةُ مَا رَأَيْتُهَا فِى الْمَنَامِ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhalat dhālika al-qaṣra wa-tafarrajat ʿalā naqshihi wa-abṣarati al-ṭuyūra wa-al-ṣayyāda wa-al-ḥamāma fa-qālat subḥāna allāhi inna hādhihi ṣiffatu mā raʾaytuhā fī al-manāmi
sentences.l: Then she entered that pavilion and looked-with-pleasure at its painting, and saw the birds and the hunter and the doves; and she said: Glory (be to) God! Indeed this (is) the likeness of what I saw it in the dream!
sentences.i: Then she went into the pavilion and gazed with delight at its paintings, and saw the birds, the fowler and the doves, and said, “Glory be to God! This is the very picture of what I saw in my dream!”
sentences.n: ṣifa, “description, likeness”: the print sets a shadda on its fāʾ (صفّة), which no reading of the word needs; the mark is kept, and we read the word as ṣifa. mā raʾaytuhā, “what I saw it”: the relative mā takes a returning pronoun, -hā, feminine as if agreeing with ṣifa. tafarraja ʿalā, “to look at for pleasure”. The print spells hādhihi with a final tāʾ marbūṭa (هذة).

sentences.t: وَصَارَتْ تَنْظُرُ إِلَى صُوَرِ الطُّيُورِ وَالصَّيَّادِ وَالشَّرَكِ وَتَتَعَجَّبُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārat tanẓuru ilā ṣuwari al-ṭuyūri wa-al-ṣayyādi wa-al-sharaki wa-tataʿajjabu
sentences.l: And she began looking at the pictures of the birds and the hunter and the net, and marvelling.
sentences.i: And she went on looking at the pictures of the birds, the fowler and the net, marvelling.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ يَا دَادَتِى إِنِّي كُنْتُ أَلُومُ الرِّجَالَ وَأُبْغِضُهُمْ وَلَكِنِ انْظُرِى الصَّيَّادَ كَيْفَ ذُبِحَتِ الطَّيْرَةُ الْأُنْثَى وَتَخَلَّصَ الذَّكَرُ وَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَجِيءَ إِلَى الْأُنْثَى وَيُخَلِّصَهَا فَقَابَلَهُ الْجَارِحُ وَافْتَرَسَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat yā dādatī innī kuntu alūmu al-rijāla wa-ubghiḍuhum wa-lākini unẓurī al-ṣayyāda kayfa dhubiḥati al-ṭayratu al-unthā wa-takhallaṣa al-dhakaru wa-arāda an yajīʾa ilā al-unthā wa-yukhalliṣahā fa-qābalahu al-jāriḥu wa-iftarasahu
sentences.l: Then she said: O my nurse, I used to blame the men and hate them; but look at the hunter: how the bird, the female, was slaughtered, and the male got-free and wanted to come to the female and free her, and the beast-of-prey met him and tore-him-as-prey.
sentences.i: Then she said, “Nanny, I used to blame men and hate them. But look at the fowler, and see how the hen bird has been slaughtered, while the cock got free and tried to come back to her and save her, and a bird of prey met him and tore him to pieces!”
sentences.n: This is not what Dunyā dreamed. In her dream the female dove freed the male from the net; but when she herself was caught, the male flew off with the other birds and never came back to her, and the fowler took her and slaughtered her — which is why she turned against men. The vizier had the painter show the female in the net under the fowler's knife and the male in the talons of a great bird of prey, so that the male's failure to return reads as death, not desertion; and Dunyā reads it just so. The print's ذبحت could be dhabaḥat, “she slaughtered”, but the fowler is a man; we take it as the passive dhubiḥat, “was slaughtered”. dāda, “nurse, nanny”, is her name for the old woman. ṭayra, a feminine of ṭayr, “bird”, is colloquial. al-jāriḥ, “the predator”, a hunting bird; iftarasa, “to seize and tear (prey)”.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتِ الْعَجُوزُ تَتَجَادَلُ عَلَيْهَا وَتُشَاغِلُهَا بِالْحَدِيثِ إِلَى أَنْ قَرُبَتَا مِنَ الْمَكَانِ الْمُخْتَفِي فِيهِ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārati al-ʿajūzu tatajādalu ʿalayhā wa-tushāghiluhā bi-al-ḥadīthi ilā an qarubatā mina al-makāni al-mukhtafī fīhi tāju al-mulūki
sentences.l: And the old woman began disputing at her and occupying her with the talk, until the two-of-them drew near to the place hiding in which (was) Tāj al-Mulūk.
sentences.i: And the old woman kept arguing the point with her and keeping her busy with talk, until the two of them came near the place where Tāj al-Mulūk lay hidden.
sentences.n: tatajādalu ʿalayhā is doubtful: tajādala is “to dispute with one another”, and with ʿalā it seems to mean that she kept arguing at her, pressing her case for men; the sense is our best reading. bi-al-ḥadīth, “with talk”: bi- of means. qarubatā, “the two (women) drew near”: a feminine dual. al-makāni al-mukhtafī fīhi tāju al-mulūki, “the place hiding in it Tāj al-Mulūk”: the participle stands with the place but takes the prince as its subject.

sentences.t: فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ الْعَجُوزُ أَنْ يَتَمَشَّى تَحْتَ شَبَابِيكِ الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-ashārat ilayhi al-ʿajūzu an yatamashshā taḥta shabābīki al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And the old woman signalled to him that he stroll under the windows of the pavilion.
sentences.i: The old woman signed to him to stroll beneath the pavilion windows.
sentences.n: shabābīk, “windows” (sing. shubbāk), usually latticed.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا كَذَلِكَ إِذْ لَاحَتْ مِنْهَا الْتِفَاتَةٌ فَرَأَتْهُ وَتَأَمَّلَتْ جَمَالَهُ وَقَدَّهُ وَاعْتِدَالَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā al-sayyidatu dunyā ka-dhālika idh lāḥat minhā iltifātatun fa-raʾathu wa-taʾammalat jamālahu wa-qaddahu wa-iʿtidālahu
sentences.l: And while the Lady Dunyā (was) thus, lo, there flashed from her a turning-glance, and she saw him and contemplated his beauty and his stature and his straightness.
sentences.i: And as the Lady Dunyā was walking so, she happened to glance aside and saw him, and looked long at his beauty, his height and his fine proportion.
sentences.n: baynamā … idh, “while … lo”. lāḥat minhā iltifāta, “a turning (of the head) flashed from her”: she chanced to look round. ka-dhālika, “thus”: ka-, “like”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ يَا دَادَتِي مِنْ أَيْنَ هَذَا الشَّابُّ الْمَلِيحُ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat yā dādatī min ayna hādhā al-shābbu al-malīḥu
sentences.l: Then she said: O my nurse, from where (is) this youth, the handsome (one)?
sentences.i: Then she said, “Nanny, where does this handsome young man come from?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَا أَعْلَمُ بِهِ غَيْرَ أَنِّي أَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ وَلَدُ مَلِكٍ عَظِيمٍ فَإِنَّهُ بَلَغَ مِنَ الْحُسْنِ النِّهَايَةَ وَمِنَ الْجَمَالِ الْغَايَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lā aʿlamu bihi ghayra annī aẓunnu annahu waladu malikin ʿaẓīmin fa-innahu balagha mina al-ḥusni al-nihāyata wa-mina al-jamāli al-ghāyata
sentences.l: And she said: I do not know of him, other than that I think that he (is) the son of a king great; for he has reached of the beauty the utmost, and of the comeliness the farthest-limit.
sentences.i: She said, “I know nothing of him, except that I think he must be the son of some great king, for he has reached the height of beauty and the very limit of grace.”
sentences.n: ʿalima bi-, “to know of”: the verb takes bi-. The print marks the shadda of aẓunnu (اظنّ). al-nihāya / al-ghāya, “the utmost / the farthest limit”, rhyme.

sentences.t: فَهَامَتْ بِهِ السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا وَانْحَلَّتْ عُرَى عَزَائِمِهَا وَانْبَهَرَ عَقْلُهَا مِنْ حُسْنِهِ وَجَمَالِهِ وَقَدِّةِ وَاعْتِدَالِهِ وَتَحَرَّكَتْ عَلَيْهَا الشَّهْوَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-hāmat bihi al-sayyidatu dunyā wa-inḥallat ʿurā ʿazāʾimihā wa-inbahara ʿaqluhā min ḥusnihi wa-jamālihi wa-qaddihi wa-iʿtidālihi wa-taḥarrakat ʿalayhā al-shahwatu
sentences.l: And the Lady Dunyā became-madly-enamoured of him, and the loops of her resolves came-undone, and her mind was dazzled by his beauty and his comeliness and his stature and his straightness, and the lust stirred upon her.
sentences.i: The Lady Dunyā fell madly in love with him: the fastenings of her resolve came undone, her mind was dazzled by his beauty and grace, his height and fine proportion, and lust stirred in her.
sentences.n: hāma bi-, “to be madly in love with”: bi- marks the beloved. ʿurā, “loops” (sing. ʿurwa), the fastenings of a garment: her resolutions came unbuttoned. The print spells qaddihi with a final tāʾ marbūṭa (قدة); read -hi. al-shahwa is plain physical desire.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِلْعَجُوزِ يَا دَادَتِي إِنَّ هَذَا الشَّابَّ مَلِيحٌ فَقَالَتْ لَهَا الْعَجُوزُ صَدَقْتِ يَاسَيِّدَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat li-al-ʿajūzi yā dādatī inna hādhā al-shābba malīḥun fa-qālat lahā al-ʿajūzu ṣadaqti yā sayyidatī
sentences.l: And she said to the old woman: O my nurse, indeed this youth (is) handsome. And the old woman said to her: You have spoken-truly, O my lady.
sentences.i: She said to the old woman, “Nanny, this young man is handsome.” “You are right, my lady,” the old woman answered.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعَجُوزَ أَشَارَتْ إِلَى ابْنِ الْمَلِكِ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ وَقَدِ الْتَهَبَتْ بِهِ نَارُ الْغَرَامِ وَزَادَ بِهِ الْوَجْدُ وَالْهُيَامُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿajūza ashārat ilā ibni al-maliki an yadhhaba ilā baytihi wa-qadi iltahabat bihi nāru al-gharāmi wa-zāda bihi al-wajdu wa-al-huyāmu
sentences.l: Then the old woman signalled to the son of the king that he go to his house — and there had blazed in him the fire of the passion, and increased in him the longing and the love-madness.
sentences.i: Then the old woman signed to the king's son to go home — though the fire of passion was blazing in him, and his longing and love-madness had grown.
sentences.n: wa-qad with the perfect describes the state he was in as he went. bihi, “in him”: bi- of place. al-gharām / al-huyām rhyme.

sentences.t: فَسَارَ وَلَمْ يَقِفْ وَوَدَّعَ الْخَوْلِيَّ وَانْصَرَفَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ وَقَدْ هَاجَ بِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ الشَّوْقُ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ لَمْ يُخَالِفِ الْعَجُوزَ
sentences.tr: fa-sāra wa-lam yaqif wa-waddaʿa al-khawliyya wa-inṣarafa ilā manzilihi wa-qad hāja bi-tāji al-mulūki al-shawqu illā annahu lam yukhālifi al-ʿajūza
sentences.l: And he went and did not stop, and bade-farewell to the gardener and departed to his lodging; and the longing had surged in Tāj al-Mulūk, except that he did not go-against the old woman.
sentences.i: So he went without lingering, took leave of the gardener and went off to his lodging; longing surged in Tāj al-Mulūk, but he would not go against the old woman.
sentences.n: al-khawlī, “the gardener”, an Egyptian word, used here alongside al-bustānī. hāja bi-, “to surge up in”: bi- of place.

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرَ الْوَزِيرَ وَعَزِيزًا بِأَنَّ الْعَجُوزَ أَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ بِالِانْصِرَافِ فَصَارَا يُصَبِّرَانِهِ وَيَقُولَانِ لَهُ لَوْلَا أَنَّ الْعَجُوزَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ فِي رُجُوعِكَ مَصْلَحَةً مَا أَشَارَتْ عَلَيْكَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhbara al-wazīra wa-ʿazīzan bi-anna al-ʿajūza ashārat ilayhi bi-al-inṣirāfi fa-ṣārā yuṣabbirānihi wa-yaqūlāni lahu lawlā anna al-ʿajūza taʿlamu anna fī rujūʿika maṣlaḥatan mā ashārat ʿalayka bihi
sentences.l: And he informed the vizier and ʿAzīz that the old woman had signalled to him to depart; so the two began making-him-patient and saying to him: Were it not that the old woman knows that in your returning (there is) a benefit, she would not have advised you to it.
sentences.i: He told the vizier and ʿAzīz that the old woman had signed to him to leave, and the two of them set about calming him, saying, “If the old woman did not know that some good would come of your going back, she would never have told you to do it.”
sentences.n: akhbara bi-, “to inform of”: the verb takes bi-. ashāra ilā … bi-, “to signal to someone to do”; ashāra ʿalā … bi-, “to advise someone to do”: the preposition changes the sense. ṣabbara, “to make patient, to console”.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَالْوَزِيرِ وَعَزِيزٍ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri tāji al-mulūki wa-al-wazīri wa-ʿazīzin
sentences.l: This (is) what was of the affair of Tāj al-Mulūk and the vizier and ʿAzīz.
sentences.i: So much for Tāj al-Mulūk, the vizier and ʿAzīz.
sentences.n: The storyteller's formula for leaving one thread of the tale to take up another. The print runs mā kāna together (ماكان).

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ بِنْتِ الْمَلِكِ السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا فَإِنَّهَا غَلَبَ عَلَيْهَا الْغَرَامُ وَزَادَ بِهَا الْوَجْدُ وَالْهُيَامُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri binti al-maliki al-sayyidati dunyā fa-innahā ghalaba ʿalayhā al-gharāmu wa-zāda bihā al-wajdu wa-al-huyāmu
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of the daughter of the king, the Lady Dunyā — she, the passion overcame her, and the longing and the love-madness increased in her.
sentences.i: As for the king's daughter, the Lady Dunyā, passion overcame her, and her longing and love-madness grew.
sentences.n: The print runs mā kāna together (ماكان). al-gharām / al-huyām is the rhyme of the sajʿ. zāda bihā, “increased in her”: bi- here is “in, upon”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِلْعَجُوزِ أَنَا مَا أَعْرِفُ اجْتِمَاعِي بِهَذَا الشَّابِّ إِلَّا مِنْكِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat li-al-ʿajūzi anā mā aʿrifu ijtimāʿī bi-hādhā al-shābbi illā minki
sentences.l: And she said to the old woman: I do not know my meeting with this young-man except from you.
sentences.i: And she said to the old woman, “I know no way to meet this young man except through you.”
sentences.n: mā aʿrifu … illā minki, “I do not know (it) except from you”: only you can bring it about. ijtimāʿ bi-, “meeting with”. The print marks the kasra of minki, “from you” (fem.).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا الْعَجُوزُ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ أَنْتِ لَا تُرِيدِينَ الرِّجَالَ وَكَيْفَ حَلَّتْ بِكِ مِنْ عِشْقِهِ الْأَ وْجَالُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā al-ʿajūzu aʿūdhu bi-allāhi mina al-shayṭāni al-rajīmi anti lā turīdīna al-rijāla wa-kayfa ḥallat biki min ʿishqihi al-awjālu
sentences.l: And the old woman said to her: I seek-refuge in God from Satan the stoned! You do not want the men — and how have the fears from love of him come-down upon you?
sentences.i: The old woman said to her, “I take refuge with God from Satan the accursed! You who will have nothing to do with men — how is it that love of him has brought such alarms down on you?
sentences.n: aʿūdhu bi-allāh, “I take refuge in God”: bi- marks the one in whom refuge is sought; the formula wards off something shocking. ḥallat bi-, “to befall, come down upon”. The print sets the last word as two, الا وجال; we read it as one word, al-awjāl, “fears, alarms”, and point it so, but the reading is not certain.

sentences.t: لَكِنْ وَاللَّهِ مَا يَصْلُحُ لِشَبَابِكِ إِلَّاهُوَ
sentences.tr: lākin wa-allāhi mā yaṣluḥu li-shabābiki illā huwa
sentences.l: But by God, not is fit for your youth except he.
sentences.i: But by God, no one is a match for your youth but him.”
sentences.n: The print runs illā huwa together (الاهو). li-, “for”: what he is fit for.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا يَا دَادَتِي أَسْعِفِينِي وَسَاعِدِينِي بِاجْتِمَاعِي عَلَيْهِ وَلَكِ عِنْدِى أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ وَخِلْعَةٌ بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-sayyidatu dunyā yā dādatī asʿifīnī wa-sāʿidīnī bi-ijtimāʿī ʿalayhi wa-laki ʿindī alfu dīnārin wa-khilʿatun bi-alfi dīnārin
sentences.l: And the Lady Dunyā said: O my nurse, succour me and help me with my meeting upon him, and for you with me (are) a thousand dinars and a robe-of-honour at a thousand dinars.
sentences.i: The Lady Dunyā said, “Nanny, help me, stand by me and bring me together with him, and you shall have from me a thousand dinars and a robe of honour worth a thousand more.
sentences.n: dāda, “nurse”, a Persian-Turkish word for the woman who brought a child up. ijtimāʿ ʿalā, “meeting with”, a Middle Arabic turn for ijtimāʿ bi-; the bi- in front, bi-ijtimāʿī, says what the help is for. bi-alfi dīnārin, “at a thousand dinars”: bi- of price. The print spells ʿindī with a final ى (عندى).

sentences.t: وَإِنْ لَمْ تُسْعِفِينِي بِوِصَالِهِ فَإِنِّي مَيِّتَةٌ لَا مَحَالَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-in lam tusʿifīnī bi-wiṣālihi fa-innī mayyitatun lā maḥālata
sentences.l: And if you do not succour me with his union, then I (am) dying, no escape.
sentences.i: If you do not help me to union with him, I shall die; there is no help for it.”
sentences.n: bi-wiṣālihi, “with union with him”: bi- marks what the help consists in. lā maḥālata, “no avoiding (it)”, that is, “inevitably”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ امْضِ أَنْتِ إِلَى قَصْرِكِ وَأَنَا أَتَسَبَّبُ فِي اجْتِمَاعِكُمَا وَأَبْذُلُ رُوحِي فِي مَرْضَاتِكُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu imḍi anti ilā qaṣriki wa-anā atasabbabu fī ijtimāʿikumā wa-abdhulu rūḥī fī marḍātikumā
sentences.l: And the old woman said: Go you to your palace, and I will make-the-means for your meeting-together, and spend my soul in your pleasing.
sentences.i: The old woman said, “Go back to your palace, and I will find a way to bring you two together, and give my very life to please you both.”
sentences.n: imḍi, “go”: the print has the masculine form امض, though she is speaking to a woman; Classical would be imḍī (امضي). tasabbaba fī, “to bring about”. ijtimāʿikumā / marḍātikumā rhyme.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ السَّيِّدَةَ دُنْيَا تَوَجَّهَتْ إِلَى قَصْرِهَا وَتَوَجَّهَتِ الْعَجُوزُ إِلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-sayyidata dunyā tawajjahat ilā qaṣrihā wa-tawajjahati al-ʿajūzu ilā tāji al-mulūki
sentences.l: Then the Lady Dunyā betook-herself to her palace, and the old woman betook-herself to Tāj al-Mulūk.
sentences.i: Then the Lady Dunyā went off to her palace, and the old woman went to Tāj al-Mulūk.
sentences.n: thumma inna, “then (it is so that)”: inna simply opens the next step of the story.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا نَهَضَ لَهَا عَلَى الْأَقْدَامِ وَقَابَلَهَا بِإِعْزَازٍ وَإِكْرَامٍ وَأَجْلَسَهَا إِلَى جَانِبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā nahaḍa lahā ʿalā al-aqdāmi wa-qābalahā bi-iʿzāzin wa-ikrāmin wa-ajlasahā ilā jānibihi
sentences.l: And when he saw her, he rose for her upon the feet, and met her with esteem and honour, and seated her at his side.
sentences.i: When he saw her he rose to his feet for her, received her with every mark of esteem and honour, and seated her beside him.
sentences.n: bi-iʿzāzin wa-ikrām, “with esteem and honour”: bi- of manner; the pair rhymes with al-aqdām.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّ الْحِيلَةَ قَدْ تَمَّتْ وَحَكَتْ لَهُ مَا جَرَى لَهَا مَعَ السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu inna al-ḥīlata qad tammat wa-ḥakat lahu mā jarā lahā maʿa al-sayyidati dunyā
sentences.l: And she said to him: The stratagem has been-completed; and she related to him what had happened to her with the Lady Dunyā.
sentences.i: She told him, “The trick has worked,” and related all that had passed between her and the Lady Dunyā.
sentences.n: The print has لها, a misprint for له (lahu), “to him”, corrected here. jarā lahā maʿa, “what happened to her with”: what passed between them.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا مَتَى يَكُونُ الِاجْتِمَاعُ قَالَتْ فِي غَدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā matā yakūnu al-ijtimāʿu qālat fī ghadin
sentences.l: And he said to her: When will be the meeting? She said: In tomorrow.
sentences.i: He asked her, “When is the meeting to be?” She said, “Tomorrow.”

sentences.t: فَأَعْطَاهَا أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَحُلَّةً بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ فَأَخَذَتْهُمَا وَانْصَرَفَتْ وَلَازَالَتْ سَائِرَةً حَتَّى دَخَلَتْ عَلَى السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا
sentences.tr: fa-aʿṭāhā alfa dīnārin wa-ḥullatan bi-alfi dīnārin fa-akhadhathumā wa-inṣarafat wa-lā zālat sāʾiratan ḥattā dakhalat ʿalā al-sayyidati dunyā
sentences.l: And he gave her a thousand dinars and a robe at a thousand dinars; and she took them-both and went-away, and did not cease going until she entered upon the Lady Dunyā.
sentences.i: He gave her a thousand dinars and a robe worth a thousand dinars; she took them both and left, and went on until she came in to the Lady Dunyā.
sentences.n: lā zālat, “she did not cease”, is run together in the print (ولازالت); lā with the past is a Middle Arabic habit for Classical mā zālat. The print marks the shadda of ḥulla, “robe”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا يَا دَادَتِي مَا عِنْدَكِ مِنْ خَبَرِ الْحَبِيبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā yā dādatī mā ʿindaki min khabari al-ḥabībi
sentences.l: And she said to her: O my nurse, what (is) with you of news of the beloved?
sentences.i: Dunyā said to her, “Nanny, what news have you of my beloved?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا قَدْ عَرَفْتُ مَكَانَهُ وَفِي غَدٍ أَكُونُ بِهِ عِنْدَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā qad ʿaraftu makānahu wa-fī ghadin akūnu bihi ʿindaki
sentences.l: And she said to her: I have known his place, and in tomorrow I will be with him with you.
sentences.i: She said to her, “I have found out where he is, and tomorrow I will have him here with you.”
sentences.n: akūnu bihi ʿindaki, “I will be with him at your side”: bi- here is “with, bringing”.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَتِ السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا بِذَلِكَ وَأَعْطَتْهَا أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَحُلَّةً بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ فَأَخَذَتْهُمَا وَانْصَرَفَتْ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهَا وَبَاتَتْ فِيهِ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥati al-sayyidatu dunyā bi-dhālika wa-aʿṭathā alfa dīnārin wa-ḥullatan bi-alfi dīnārin fa-akhadhathumā wa-inṣarafat ilā manzilihā wa-bātat fīhi ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And the Lady Dunyā rejoiced at that, and gave her a thousand dinars and a robe at a thousand dinars; and she took them-both and went-away to her dwelling and passed-the-night in it until the morning.
sentences.i: The Lady Dunyā was delighted at this and gave her a thousand dinars and a robe worth a thousand dinars; the old woman took them both, went home and stayed there overnight till morning.
sentences.n: fariḥa bi-, “to rejoice at”: the verb takes bi-. The old woman is now paid the same by both lovers.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجَتْ وَتَوَجَّهَتْ إِلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَأَلْبَسَتْهُ لِبْسَ النِّسَاءِ
sentences.tr: thumma kharajat wa-tawajjahat ilā tāji al-mulūki wa-albasathu libsa al-nisāʾi
sentences.l: Then she went-out and betook-herself to Tāj al-Mulūk, and clothed him (in) the dress of the women.
sentences.i: Then she went out to Tāj al-Mulūk and dressed him in women's clothes.
sentences.n: albasahu libsa, “to clothe someone in”: the verb takes two objects.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ امْشِ خَلْفِي وَتَمَايَلْ فِي خَطَوَاتِكَ وَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلْ فِي مَشْيِكَ وَلَا تَلْتَفِتْ إِلَى مَنْ يُكَلِّمُكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu imshi khalfī wa-tamāyal fī khaṭawātika wa-lā tastaʿjil fī mashyika wa-lā taltafit ilā man yukallimuka
sentences.l: And she said to him: Walk behind me, and sway in your steps, and do not hurry in your walking, and do not turn to whoever speaks-to-you.
sentences.i: And she told him, “Walk behind me and sway as you step; don't hurry as you walk, and don't turn round for anyone who speaks to you.”
sentences.n: The print points tamāyal, “sway”, with its own vowels (تَمَايَلْ), so that it is read as an imperative: he is to walk like a woman.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ أَنْ أَوْصَتْ تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ بِهَذِهِ الْوَصِيَّةِ خَرَجَتْ وَخَرَجَ خَلْفَهَا وَهُوَ فِي زِيِّ النِّسْوَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda an awṣat tāja al-mulūki bi-hādhihi al-waṣiyyati kharajat wa-kharaja khalfahā wa-huwa fī ziyyi al-niswāni
sentences.l: And after she had charged Tāj al-Mulūk with this charge, she went-out, and he went-out behind her, and he (was) in the guise of the women.
sentences.i: When she had given Tāj al-Mulūk these instructions she went out, and he went out behind her in women's dress.
sentences.n: awṣāhu bi-, “to charge someone with”: the verb takes bi-. niswān, “women”, a by-form of nisāʾ.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتْ تُعَلِّمُهُ وَتُجَسِّرُهُ فِى الطَّرِيقِ حَتَّى لَا يَفْزَعَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārat tuʿallimuhu wa-tujassiruhu fī al-ṭarīqi ḥattā lā yafzaʿa
sentences.l: And she began teaching him and emboldening him on the way, so-that he not take-fright.
sentences.i: All along the way she coached him and kept his courage up, so that he would not lose his nerve.
sentences.n: jassara, “to embolden”. The print spells fī with a final ى (فى).

sentences.t: وَلَمْ تَزَلْ مَاشِيَةً وَهُوَ خَلْفَهَا حَتَّى وَصَلَا إِلَى بَابِ الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam tazal māshiyatan wa-huwa khalfahā ḥattā waṣalā ilā bābi al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And she did not cease walking, and he behind her, until they-two arrived at the gate of the palace.
sentences.i: She walked on, with him behind her, until the two of them reached the palace gate.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَتْ وَهُوَ وَرَاءَهَا وَصَارَتْ تَخْتَرِقُ الْأَبْوَابَ وَالدَّهَالِيزَ إِلَى أَنْ جَاوَزَتْ بِهِ سَبْعَةَ أَبْوَابٍ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalat wa-huwa warāʾahā wa-ṣārat takhtariqu al-abwāba wa-al-dahālīza ilā an jāwazat bihi sabʿata abwābin
sentences.l: And she entered, and he behind her, and she began passing-through the doors and the passages until she had passed with him seven doors.
sentences.i: She went in with him behind her, and threaded her way through door after door and passage after passage until she had brought him past seven doors.
sentences.n: The print has الا, a misprint for الى (ilā an, “until”), corrected here. jāwaza bihi, “to take him past”: bi- “with” makes the verb carry him along. dihlīz, plural dahālīz, “passage, vestibule”, is from Persian.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا وَصَلَتْ إِلَى الْبَابِ السَّابِعِ قَالَتْ لِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ قَوِّ قَلْبَكَ وَإِذَا زَعَقْتُ عَلَيْكَ وَقُلْتُ لَكَ يَا جَارِيَةُ اعْبُرِى فَلَا تَتَوَانَ فِي مَشْيِكَ وَهَرْوِلْ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā waṣalat ilā al-bābi al-sābiʿi qālat li-tāji al-mulūki qawwi qalbaka wa-idhā zaʿaqtu ʿalayka wa-qultu laka yā jāriyatu uʿburī fa-lā tatawāna fī mashyika wa-harwil
sentences.l: And when she arrived at the door the seventh, she said to Tāj al-Mulūk: Strengthen your heart; and when I shout at you and say to you, “O slave-girl, pass-through!”, then do not slacken in your walking, and trot.
sentences.i: When she reached the seventh door she said to Tāj al-Mulūk, “Take heart! When I shout at you, ‘Go on through, girl!’, don't dawdle: hurry along.
sentences.n: The print points several words here itself: qawwi (قوّ), zaʿaqtu (زعقتُ) and harwil (هَرْوِلْ), “trot, hurry along”. zaʿaqa ʿalā, “to shout at”, is colloquial. uʿburī, “pass through”, is feminine, as befits the slave-girl he is playing; the print spells it with a final ى. lā tatawāna, “do not slacken”, from tawānā.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا دَخَلْتَ الدِّهْلِيزَ فَانْظُرْ إِلَى شِمَالِكَ تَرَى إِيوَانًا فِيهِ أَبْوَابٌ فَعُدَّ خَمْسَةَ أَبْوَابٍ وَادْخُلِ الْبَابَ السَّادِسَ فَإِنَّ مُرَادَكَ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā dakhalta al-dihlīza fa-unẓur ilā shimālika tarā īwānan fīhi abwābun fa-ʿudda khamsata abwābin wa-udkhuli al-bāba al-sādisa fa-inna murādaka fīhi
sentences.l: And when you enter the passage, look to your left: you will see a hall in which (are) doors; so count five doors and enter the door the sixth, for your desire (is) in it.
sentences.i: When you are in the passage, look to your left and you will see a hall with doors in it. Count five doors and go in at the sixth, for what you long for is there.”
sentences.n: tarā, “you will see”: after an imperative Classical Arabic would use the short form tara; the print keeps the long one. īwān, “a hall open on one side”, is from Persian. murād, “what is wished for”, here the Lady Dunyā herself. The print marks the shadda of ʿudda, “count”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَأَيْنَ تَرُوحِينَ أَنْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla tāju al-mulūki wa-ayna tarūḥīna anti
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk said: And where do you go, you?
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk said, “And where will you be going?”
sentences.n: rāḥa, “to go”, is the everyday verb of going, here and in her answer.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ مَا أَرُوحُ مَوْضِعًا غَيْرَ أَنِّي رُبَّمَا أَتَأَخَّرُ عَنْكَ وَعَاقَنِى الْخَادِمُ الْكَبِيرُ وَأَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu mā arūḥu mawḍiʿan ghayra annī rubbamā ataʾakhkharu ʿanka wa-ʿāqanī al-khādimu al-kabīru wa-ataḥaddathu maʿahu
sentences.l: And she said to him: I do not go (to) a place; except that I perhaps lag-behind you, and the servant the great detained-me, and I talk with him.
sentences.i: She said, “I am going nowhere. Only I may fall behind you, if the chief eunuch holds me up and I stop to talk with him.”
sentences.n: arūḥu mawḍiʿan, “go (to) a place”, with the place as a bare object, is colloquial. ʿāqanī, “detains me”, is past in form but looks ahead, after rubbamā; the print spells it with a final ى (عاقنى). al-khādim al-kabīr, “the great servant”, is the chief eunuch who keeps the palace doors.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَشَتْ وَهُوَ خَلْفَهَا حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ إِلَى الْبَابِ الَّذِى فِيهِ الْخَادِمُ الْكَبِيرُ
sentences.tr: thumma mashat wa-huwa khalfahā ḥattā waṣalat ilā al-bābi alladhī fīhi al-khādimu al-kabīru
sentences.l: Then she walked, and he behind her, until she arrived at the door which in it (was) the servant the great.
sentences.i: Then she walked on with him behind her until she reached the door where the chief eunuch was.
sentences.n: The print spells alladhī with a final ى (الذى).

sentences.t: فَرَأَى مَعَهَا تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ فِي صُورَةِ جَارِيَةٍ فَقَالَ لَهَا مَا شَأْنُ هَذِةِ الْجَارِيَةِ الَّتِي مَعَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾā maʿahā tāja al-mulūki fī ṣūrati jāriyatin fa-qāla lahā mā shaʾnu hādhihi al-jāriyati allatī maʿaki
sentences.l: And he saw with her Tāj al-Mulūk in the form of a slave-girl, and said to her: What (is) the affair of this slave-girl who (is) with you?
sentences.i: He saw Tāj al-Mulūk with her in the shape of a slave-girl and said to her, “What about this girl you have with you?”
sentences.n: The print spells hādhihi with a final tāʾ marbūṭa (هذة), here and in the next sentence.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ هَذِةِ جَارِيَةٌ قَدْ سَمِعَتِ السَّيِّدَةُ دُنْيَا بِأَنَّهَا تَعْرِفُ الْأَشْغَالَ وَتُرِيدُأَنْ تَشْتَرِيَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu hādhihi jāriyatun qad samiʿati al-sayyidatu dunyā bi-annahā taʿrifu al-ashghāla wa-turīdu an tashtariyahā
sentences.l: And she said to him: This (is) a slave-girl; the Lady Dunyā has heard of-that she knows the works, and wants that she buy her.
sentences.i: She told him, “This is a slave-girl. The Lady Dunyā has heard that she is skilled at handiwork, and wants to buy her.”
sentences.n: samiʿa bi-, “to hear of”: the verb takes bi-. al-ashghāl, “works”, here the handicrafts of a skilled slave-girl, such as embroidery. The print runs turīdu an together (وتريدان).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا الْخَادِمُ أَنَا لَا أَعْرِفُ جَارِيَةً وَلَا غَيْرَهَا وَلَا يَدْخُلُ أَحَدٌ حَتَّى أُفَتِّشَهُ كَمَا أَمَرَنِي الْمَلِكُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-khādimu anā lā aʿrifu jāriyatan wa-lā ghayrahā wa-lā yadkhulu aḥadun ḥattā ufattishahu kamā amaranī al-maliku
sentences.l: And the servant said to her: I do not know a slave-girl nor other-than-her; and no one enters until I search him, as the king commanded me.
sentences.i: The eunuch said to her, “Slave-girl or no slave-girl, it is all one to me: nobody goes in until I have searched them, as the king has ordered me.”
sentences.n: lā aʿrifu jāriyatan wa-lā ghayrahā, “I know neither slave-girl nor anything else”: it makes no difference to him who she is. The print marks the shadda of ufattishahu, “I search him”.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The print sets Shahrazād as two words (شهر زاد).
